gsod_daily_cleaned.name: gsod_daily_cleaned
gsod_daily_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  stn AS stn,
  wban AS wban,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year, '-', LPAD(mo, 2, '0'), '-', LPAD(da, 2, '0'))) AS obs_date,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN temp IS NULL OR temp = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE temp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS temp_f,
  count_temp AS count_temp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN dewp IS NULL OR dewp = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE dewp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS dewp_f,
  count_dewp AS count_dewp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN slp IS NULL OR slp = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE slp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS slp_mbar,
  count_slp AS count_slp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN stp IS NULL OR stp = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE stp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS stp_mbar,
  count_stp AS count_stp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN visib IS NULL OR visib = 999.9 THEN NULL ELSE visib END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS visib_miles,
  count_visib AS count_visib,
  -- wdsp and count_wdsp are strings in the DDL; attempt safe cast to float/int
  NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(wdsp AS FLOAT64), 999.9) AS wdsp_knots,
  SAFE_CAST(count_wdsp AS INT64) AS count_wdsp,
  NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(mxpsd AS FLOAT64), 999.9) AS mxpsd_knots,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN gust IS NULL OR gust = 999.9 THEN NULL ELSE gust END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS gust_knots,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN max IS NULL OR max = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE max END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS max_f,
  flag_max AS flag_max,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN min IS NULL OR min = 9999.9 THEN NULL ELSE min END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS min_f,
  flag_min AS flag_min,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN prcp IS NULL OR prcp = 99.99 THEN NULL ELSE prcp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS prcp_inches,
  flag_prcp AS flag_prcp,
  NULLIF(CASE WHEN sndp IS NULL OR sndp = 999.9 THEN NULL ELSE sndp END, CAST(NULL AS FLOAT64)) AS sndp_inches,
  -- weather occurrence indicators kept as-is (string '1'/'0' or NULL)
  fog AS fog,
  rain_drizzle AS rain_drizzle,
  snow_ice_pellets AS snow_ice_pellets,
  hail AS hail,
  thunder AS thunder,
  tornado_funnel_cloud AS tornado_funnel_cloud,
  -- source shard year for filtering across wildcard tables
  year AS obs_year,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.gsod*`
grain: stn, wban, obs_date  -- one row per station per calendar day (cleaned)

semantic_filters.table_suffix: use WHEN querying a year range via _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN 'YYYY' AND 'YYYY' or other shard filter; do not select a single shard unless intended

gsod_daily_cleaned.description: Normalize and clean GSOD daily observations across year shards: assemble a DATE, convert sentinel missing values to NULL, cast wind fields stored as STRING, and preserve station identifiers for joins. Use this when you need cleaned daily weather measures or to join GSOD to stations or other datasets. | Use for: Daily temperature, precipitation, wind or visibility time series for a station or region; Join cleaned GSOD daily measures to stations for mapping or aggregation; Compute monthly/yearly aggregates while ignoring sentinel missing values; Filter days with precipitation or specific weather occurrences (fog, thunder, etc.)

stations_dim.name: stations_dim
stations_dim.body_sql:
SELECT
  usaf AS usaf,
  wban AS wban,
  name AS station_name,
  country AS country,
  state AS state,
  call AS call_sign,
  SAFE_CAST(lat AS FLOAT64) AS lat,
  SAFE_CAST(lon AS FLOAT64) AS lon,
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(elev, '') AS FLOAT64) AS elev,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', begin) AS begin_date,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', `end`) AS end_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
grain: usaf, wban  -- one row per station identifier

semantic_filters.none: Do not filter here; keep full stations dimension. Downstream queries may restrict by country/state or active date ranges.

params.description: Normalized stations dimension: one row per station identifier (usaf, wban) with canonical station name, location, elevation and active date range.
params.when_to_use: Lookup station metadata (name, country, state, call sign) for a given usaf/wban identifier. | Enrich weather/observation rows with station lat/lon/elevation and operational date range for joins by station id. | Filter or aggregate observations by station attributes (country, state) or by station active period. | Compose into larger queries that need a stable, one-row-per-station reference for joining to time-series event/observation tables.
params.output_schema: usaf: Station USAF identifier (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.usaf). | wban: Station WBAN identifier (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.wban). | station_name: Human-readable station name (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.name). | country: Country code for the station (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.country). | state: State code for the station (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.state). | call_sign: Station call sign (derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.call). | lat: Latitude as FLOAT64 (SAFE_CAST of bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.lat). | lon: Longitude as FLOAT64 (SAFE_CAST of bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.lon). | elev: Elevation as FLOAT64 (SAFE_CAST of NULLIF(bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.elev, '') ). | begin_date: Station begin date as DATE (PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.begin)). | end_date: Station end date as DATE (PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.end)).
params.metric: lat = SAFE_CAST(bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.lat AS FLOAT64) | lon = SAFE_CAST(bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.lon AS FLOAT64) | elev = SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.elev, '') AS FLOAT64) | begin_date = PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.begin) | end_date = PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations.end)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: Join to time-series or observation tables keyed by (usaf, wban) — for example gsod_daily_cleaned (normalized daily observations) — on stations_dim.usaf = gsod_daily_cleaned.usaf AND stations_dim.wban = gsod_daily_cleaned.wban. This is safe because stations_dim is one-row-per-(usaf,wban) (dimension) so joining will not duplicate station-level attributes; the observation table can have many rows per station but that multiplicity is expected. | cardinality-SAFE: Join to sibling normalized event views that reference a single station id per event (for example events_point_reports_normalized) on (usaf, wban) — safe for enrichment because stations_dim provides one row per id. | not-safe-to-join-directly-withOUT-aggregation: Do NOT join stations_dim to any one-to-many aggregated view or table that itself has multiple rows per (usaf,wban) (for example a per-station-per-day aggregated table) if you intend to preserve station-level deduplicated measures; such joins will multiplicatively increase row counts. Instead either (a) aggregate the one-to-many side to one row per (usaf,wban) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate explicitly, e.g., GROUP BY stations_dim.usaf, stations_dim.wban after the join. | examples of unsafe targets: any AGG/RANK/WIN/SET/RESHAPE sibling that produces multiple rows per station identifier (for example tornado_paths_enriched_by_date, storm_peak_intensity_rank, icoads_ship_observation_sequences_win) — these should be joined only after understanding their grain or by aggregating them to station-level. | key guidance: treat (usaf,wban) as the natural composite key. If joining on only one identifier (usaf OR wban) ensure the other identifier is handled consistently (nulls or missing) because stations_dim's uniqueness is defined over the pair. If you need to join by geographic proximity instead of id, do not use this view as an aggregation source; use lat/lon for spatial joins and then re-aggregate as needed.

stations_dim.description: Clean stations dimension with standardized column names and parsed numeric lat/lon/elevation and parsed begin/end dates. Use for joins to GSOD or for spatial lookups. | Use for: Lookup station metadata for display or mapping; Join stations to GSOD cleaned daily observations by stn/usaf and wban; Filter stations by country/state or active date ranges

events_point_reports_normalized.name: events_point_reports_normalized
events_point_reports_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  event_source,
  timestamp AS event_timestamp,
  DATE(timestamp) AS event_date,
  time AS event_hour_string,
  -- canonical numeric measure: wind.speed, hail.size (hundredths of inch), tornado.f_scale (left as original string)
  CASE WHEN event_source = 'wind_reports' THEN CAST(speed AS INT64)
       WHEN event_source = 'hail_reports' THEN CAST(size AS INT64)
       WHEN event_source = 'tornado_reports' THEN NULL
       ELSE NULL END AS severity_measure,
  -- original severity text where applicable
  CASE WHEN event_source = 'tornado_reports' THEN f_scale
       ELSE NULL END AS severity_text,
  location,
  county,
  state,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  comments,
  report_point
FROM (
  -- wind reports across shards
  SELECT 'wind_reports' AS event_source, timestamp, time, speed, NULL AS size, NULL AS f_scale, location, county, state, latitude, longitude, comments, report_point
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.wind_reports*`
  UNION ALL
  -- hail reports across shards
  SELECT 'hail_reports' AS event_source, timestamp, time, NULL AS speed, size, NULL AS f_scale, location, county, state, latitude, longitude, comments, report_point
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.hail_reports*`
  UNION ALL
  -- tornado reports across shards
  SELECT 'tornado_reports' AS event_source, timestamp, time, NULL AS speed, NULL AS size, f_scale, location, county, state, latitude, longitude, comments, report_point
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.tornado_reports*`
)
grain: event_source, event_timestamp, latitude, longitude  -- one row per original report event

params.description: Normalized, one-row-per-original severe-weather report (wind, hail, tornado) with a canonical numeric severity_measure and original severity_text, plus location, time, and free-text comments.
params.when_to_use: Produce a cleaned, unified feed of individual original severe-storm reports (wind, hail, tornado) for filtering, mapping, or time-series counting at the report level. | Aggregate counts or simple statistics (e.g., average wind speed, max hail size) by date, hour, county, state, or spatial buckets by composing GROUP BY on this view. | Join to a spatial or administrative lookup (county/state geometry, station metadata) when each original report should remain one row and not be multiplied by the lookup. | Compose into downstream views that compute event-level metrics (counts, sums, min/max) because the view exposes canonical numeric measure(s) and raw text severity per report.
params.output_schema: event_source: string — source dataset identifier for the original report; derives from the literal labels assigned in each UNION branch ('wind_reports', 'hail_reports', 'tornado_reports'). | event_timestamp: timestamp — original report timestamp column (aliased from timestamp in the source shards). | event_date: date — DATE(event_timestamp), derived from the source timestamp column. | event_hour_string: string — time-of-day string (aliased from time in the source shards); preserves original time formatting from the source. | severity_measure: int64|null — canonical numeric severity measure: for wind_reports this is CAST(speed AS INT64); for hail_reports this is CAST(size AS INT64) (hail size is stored in hundredths of an inch per the view comment); for tornado_reports this is NULL (no numeric canonicalized value). | severity_text: string|null — original textual severity where applicable: for tornado_reports this is f_scale (original F-scale text). | location: string|null — original location text from the source (aliased from location). | county: string|null — original county text from the source (aliased from county). | state: string|null — original state text from the source (aliased from state). | latitude: numeric|null — report latitude from the source (aliased from latitude). | longitude: numeric|null — report longitude from the source (aliased from longitude). | comments: string|null — free-text comments from the source (aliased from comments). | report_point: GEOGRAPHY|string|null — original report_point geometry or representation from the source (aliased from report_point).
params.metric: severity_measure = CASE WHEN event_source = 'wind_reports' THEN CAST(speed AS INT64) WHEN event_source = 'hail_reports' THEN CAST(size AS INT64) WHEN event_source = 'tornado_reports' THEN NULL ELSE NULL END | severity_text = CASE WHEN event_source = 'tornado_reports' THEN f_scale ELSE NULL END | event_date = DATE(event_timestamp)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional or one-row-per-geography tables (e.g., a state/county geometry table keyed by (state, county)) ON state = state AND county = county — safe because this view is one-row-per-original-report and county/state lookup is one-row-per-county, so measures from this view are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a stations or single-row-per-station view (e.g., stations_dim keyed by station_id) only if you first ensure a one-to-one match key on this view (this view does not expose station_id by default). | do NOT directly join this view to true one-to-many tables or views (for example: a many-row per report attachments table, or a path/segment table such as tornado_paths_enriched_by_date which represents multi-segment geometries per event) without aggregation — joining a one-to-many child will multiply report rows and thus duplicate counts/sums derived from severity_measure. If you need to combine with a one-to-many child, either: | - aggregate the child to one row per report (e.g., per report identifier or per event_timestamp+location) before joining, or | - aggregate this view after the join (GROUP BY the original report key) to re-summarize measures. | When composing aggregates: treat this view as the atomic report-level grain (event_source, event_timestamp, latitude, longitude). Any join that preserves that grain (one-to-one or many-to-one into this view) will not duplicate measures; any join that expands rows per that grain must be followed by a re-aggregation to avoid measure inflation.

events_point_reports_normalized.description: Normalize and unify point-based event reports (wind, hail, tornado reports shards) into a common schema with consistent timestamp/date, event_type, severity measure and location columns. Useful as a canonical input for aggregations, spatial joins, or time-series analyses across report types. | Use for: time series counts or rates of reports by day/state/event type; top-k highest wind speeds or largest hail sizes over a period; spatial joins to forecast regions or mapping/report clustering; filtering by event_type and computing summary statistics

tornado_paths_enriched_by_date.name: tornado_paths_enriched_by_date
tornado_paths_enriched_by_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  storm_date,
  state_name,
  state_abbreviation,
  state_fips_code,
  COUNT(1) AS paths_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(length, 0.0)) AS total_length_miles,
  AVG(NULLIF(length, 0)) AS avg_length_miles,
  SUM(COALESCE(injured_count, 0)) AS total_injured,
  SUM(COALESCE(fatality_count, 0)) AS total_fatalities,
  SUM(COALESCE(width, 0)) AS total_width_feet,
  -- preserve an ordering rank per date for selecting top N by length downstream
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY storm_date ORDER BY SUM(COALESCE(length, 0.0)) DESC) AS rank_by_length_per_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.tornado_paths`
GROUP BY storm_date, state_name, state_abbreviation, state_fips_code

params.description: Daily, state-level aggregates of tornado path counts, lengths, injuries, fatalities, and widths, with a per-date ranking by total path length.
params.when_to_use: Get counts and summary measures of tornado paths for a specific date and state (e.g., How many tornado paths and total length occurred in Iowa on 2015-05-25?). | Compare states on a given storm_date by total tornado path length or rank (e.g., list top N states by total tornado path length for a date). | Time-series analysis at daily granularity per state when using storm_date as the time key (e.g., trends of total_length_miles or total_injured by state over time). | As an aggregated building-block when composing higher-level reports that need one row per (storm_date, state) (e.g., join to a state population dimension to compute per-capita impact). | Filter for top-ranked states per date (using rank_by_length_per_date) before joining to other datasets for detail-level enrichment (but avoid joining to detail tables without re-aggregation).
params.output_schema: storm_date: calendar date of the storm event grouping — sourced from tornado_paths.storm_date | state_name: full state name for the path grouping — sourced from tornado_paths.state_name | state_abbreviation: postal state code (e.g., 'IA') for the grouping — sourced from tornado_paths.state_abbreviation | state_fips_code: state FIPS code string/number used for the grouping — sourced from tornado_paths.state_fips_code | paths_count: COUNT(1) — number of tornado path records aggregated into this (storm_date, state) row; derived from COUNT(1) over tornado_paths rows | total_length_miles: SUM(COALESCE(length, 0.0)) — sum of the length column (in miles) across tornado_paths rows for the group; sourced from tornado_paths.length | avg_length_miles: AVG(NULLIF(length, 0)) — average of non-zero length values (NULLs and zeros handled) across tornado_paths rows for the group; sourced from tornado_paths.length | total_injured: SUM(COALESCE(injured_count, 0)) — total injured persons summed from tornado_paths.injured_count across the group | total_fatalities: SUM(COALESCE(fatality_count, 0)) — total fatalities summed from tornado_paths.fatality_count across the group | total_width_feet: SUM(COALESCE(width, 0)) — sum of the width (in feet) across tornado_paths rows for the group; sourced from tornado_paths.width | rank_by_length_per_date: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY storm_date ORDER BY SUM(COALESCE(length,0.0)) DESC) — per-storm_date rank ordering states by total_length_miles (ties get same rank); computed from the grouped SUM(length)
params.metric: paths_count = COUNT(1) over rows grouped by (storm_date, state_name, state_abbreviation, state_fips_code) | total_length_miles = SUM(COALESCE(length, 0.0)) over grouped rows | avg_length_miles = AVG(NULLIF(length, 0)) over grouped rows (note: zeros excluded via NULLIF; NULLs are ignored by AVG) | total_injured = SUM(COALESCE(injured_count, 0)) over grouped rows | total_fatalities = SUM(COALESCE(fatality_count, 0)) over grouped rows | total_width_feet = SUM(COALESCE(width, 0)) over grouped rows | rank_by_length_per_date = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY storm_date ORDER BY SUM(COALESCE(length,0.0)) DESC) — computed from total_length_miles per state within each storm_date
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a state dimension (e.g., a states_dim view keyed by state_abbreviation or state_fips_code) on state_abbreviation or state_fips_code — safe because this view is one row per (storm_date, state) and the state dimension is one row per state, so measures (paths_count, totals) will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a calendar/date dimension on storm_date — safe because calendar dimensions are one row per date and will not multiply aggregated measures. | do NOT join directly to the base tornado_paths table (or any other tornado-path-level/detail table) without re-aggregating the detail side first — joining a one-row-per-(storm_date,state) aggregated view to multiple detail rows will multiply the aggregated measures (double-counting totals). If you need path-level detail together with these aggregates, either: (a) join the detail table aggregated to the same grouping before joining (re-aggregate by storm_date + state), or (b) join detail rows and recompute aggregates from detail after the join. | do NOT join to any one-to-many table (e.g., multiple event reports, station observations, or other detail-level events) using only storm_date or state as the key unless that other side is pre-aggregated to the same grain. Example unsafe joins: joining to events_point_reports_normalized on storm_date will duplicate this view's measures when multiple reports exist for the same date/state. | safe composition for ranking queries: to get top N states by total_length_miles per date, filter on rank_by_length_per_date (e.g., WHERE rank_by_length_per_date <= N) and then join to other one-row-per-state/date resources (like state metadata). Avoid joining to multi-row detail tables after applying the rank filter unless re-aggregation is performed. | when joining to other AGG views that are also one-row-per-(storm_date, state) and use the same grouping keys, the join is safe (measures align row-for-row). Always verify the other view's declared grain matches (storm_date, state_name, state_abbreviation, state_fips_code). | if you need to combine measures from this view with measures from a different grain (for example, county-level or path-level), bring both sides to a common aggregation grain explicitly (e.g., aggregate path-level data up to storm_date+state before joining) to preserve correct totals.

tornado_paths_enriched_by_date.description: Aggregate tornado_paths to produce per-day and per-state summaries (counts, total length, total injuries/fatalities) and include a running rank of paths by length within each date. Useful for daily/state-level reporting of tornado impact and for selecting top-N paths by length per day. | Use for: daily/state tornado burden (counts, injuries, fatalities, lengths); identify top-N longest tornado paths per day (use rank_by_length_per_date <= K); compare average/total path lengths across states or dates

hurricane_track_points_core.name: hurricane_track_points_core
hurricane_track_points_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  season,
  number,
  basin,
  subbasin,
  name,
  iso_time,
  nature,
  -- canonical lat/lon (use primary latitude/longitude columns present in table)
  latitude,
  longitude,
  -- WMO reported measures
  wmo_wind,
  wmo_pressure,
  wmo_agency,
  -- distance / landfall indicators
  dist2land,
  landfall,
  -- track provenance and type
  track_type,
  iflag,
  usa_agency,
  -- USA agency measures
  usa_latitude,
  usa_longitude,
  usa_status,
  usa_wind,
  usa_pressure,
  usa_sshs,
  usa_rmw,
  -- Tokyo (JMA) measures
  tokyo_latitude,
  tokyo_longitude,
  tokyo_grade,
  tokyo_wind,
  tokyo_pressure,
  tokyo_land,
  -- CMA measures
  cma_latitude,
  cma_longitude,
  cma_cat,
  cma_wind,
  cma_pressure,
  -- Reunion measures
  reunion_latitude,
  reunion_longitude,
  reunion_type,
  reunion_wind,
  reunion_pressure,
  reunion_tnum,
  reunion_ci,
  -- ISO date parts for easy partitioning/aggregation
  EXTRACT(DATE FROM iso_time) AS obs_date,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM iso_time) AS obs_year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM iso_time) AS obs_month,
  EXTRACT(DAY FROM iso_time) AS obs_day
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
grain: sid, iso_time -- one row per track observation (storm id + timestamp)
hurricane_track_points_core.description: Normalized, cleaned projection of the raw hurricanes table keeping canonical storm identifiers, primary timestamp, canonical lat/lon, common intensity measures from major agencies, and provenance flags. Use this as the base relation for most analyses (filtering, aggregation, windowing, joins). | Use for: Filter track points by basin/season/time range; Compare measures across agencies at same observation time; Aggregate max/min/mean wind or pressure per storm or season; Map storm tracks using canonical lat/lon

storm_peak_intensity_rank.name: storm_peak_intensity_rank
storm_peak_intensity_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  season,
  number,
  name,
  iso_time,
  -- preserve canonical coords and primary measures
  latitude,
  longitude,
  wmo_wind,
  usa_wind,
  usa_pressure,
  tokyo_wind,
  cma_wind,
  -- rank of observation within storm by descending usa_wind then descending wmo_wind then earliest time
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC) AS rank_by_usa_wind,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC) AS rownum_by_usa_wind
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
grain: sid, iso_time -- one row per track observation augmented with per-storm rank

params.description: Per-storm observation rows augmented with an intra-storm rank by peak intensity using USA wind (then WMO wind, then earliest time) — one row per hurricane track observation with position, agency measures, and rank within that storm.
params.when_to_use: Find the strongest observation(s) for each storm according to the 'usa_wind' measure (e.g., peak wind observation per storm). | Compose queries to select top-N observations per storm (e.g., top 1 observation per sid) based on usa_wind with deterministic tie-breaking. | Join storm observation-level attributes (location, time, multiple agency measures) with a per-storm rank to filter or aggregate only peak observations. | Produce storm-level summaries by selecting rows with rank_by_usa_wind = 1 (or other rank thresholds) and then aggregating across storms (seasonal counts, max winds, etc.).
params.output_schema: sid: storm identifier — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.sid | season: storm season/year — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.season | number: storm number within season — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.number | name: storm name — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.name | iso_time: observation timestamp (ISO) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.iso_time | latitude: canonical observation latitude — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.latitude | longitude: canonical observation longitude — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.longitude | wmo_wind: WMO-reported wind speed at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.wmo_wind | usa_wind: USA/NHC-reported wind speed at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.usa_wind | usa_pressure: USA/NHC-reported pressure at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.usa_pressure | tokyo_wind: Tokyo agency-reported wind speed at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.tokyo_wind | cma_wind: CMA (China) reported wind speed at this observation (nullable) — sourced from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.cma_wind | rank_by_usa_wind: RANK() over partition by sid ordered by usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC — 1 = highest usa_wind (ties produce same rank) | rownum_by_usa_wind: ROW_NUMBER() over same ordering — unique sequence number per observation within the storm (no ties)
params.metric: rank_by_usa_wind = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC) | rownum_by_usa_wind = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY usa_wind DESC NULLS LAST, wmo_wind DESC NULLS LAST, iso_time ASC)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension-like tables keyed by sid (for example a storm-level summary) on sid — safe because this view is one row per original observation (partitioned by sid) and joining a single-row-per-sid table will not duplicate per-observation rows when the dim is truly one-row-per-sid. | You can safely join this view to a storm-level table/view that has exactly one row per sid (e.g., a validated 'storm' master table keyed by sid) using: ON storm.sid = storm_peak_intensity_rank.sid — this will not multiply measures because the master storm table is one-to-one with sid. | Do NOT blindly join this view to any table/view that is one-to-many with respect to sid (for example: track points, multiple observation sources, station reports, or any per-observation enrichment) without first aggregating or deduplicating the other side, because doing so will multiply rows and duplicate rank/measure values. If you must join to a one-to-many relation, either: | - aggregate the other relation to one row per (sid, iso_time) or one row per sid before joining, or | - join on both sid and iso_time (or rownum_by_usa_wind if you selected a specific rank) to preserve row-level alignment and avoid duplication. | Examples of unsafe joins (may duplicate measures): joining to hurricane_track_points_core (if it contains multiple rows per sid and iso_time) without disambiguation; joining to any AGG/SET/RESHAPE sibling that produces multiple rows per sid. | To extract storm peaks safely: filter this view WHERE rank_by_usa_wind = 1 (or rownum_by_usa_wind = 1) to get a single observation per storm, then join that filtered result to other one-row-per-sid tables or aggregate the join target to per-sid before joining.

storm_peak_intensity_rank.description: Per-storm ranked observations ordered by descending chosen intensity measure (usa_wind as default) and by iso_time to break ties. Exposes rank so downstream queries can select top-K peak observations per storm (e.g., time of peak intensity). | Use for: Find time and location of peak intensity per storm; Select top-K strongest observations per storm; Rank storms by their maximum reported wind when aggregated

storm_observation_deltas_win.name: storm_observation_deltas_win
storm_observation_deltas_win.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  season,
  number,
  iso_time,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  usa_latitude,
  usa_longitude,
  usa_wind,
  LAG(iso_time) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS prev_iso_time,
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(iso_time, LAG(iso_time) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time), SECOND) AS seconds_since_prev,
  -- geographic displacement using canonical lat/lon in degrees (consumer may convert to km/nautical miles externally)
  latitude - LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS delta_lat_deg,
  longitude - LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS delta_lon_deg,
  -- delta in reporting agency wind
  usa_wind - LAG(usa_wind) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) AS delta_usa_wind,
  -- simple speed proxy: degrees per second (not true geodesic) exposed for downstream conversion
  SAFE_DIVIDE( SQRT( POW(latitude - LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time), 2) + POW(longitude - LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time), 2) ),
    NULLIF(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(iso_time, LAG(iso_time) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time), SECOND), 0)
  ) AS deg_per_second
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
grain: sid, iso_time -- one row per track observation with differences to previous observation for same storm

params.description: Per-storm-observation deltas: one row per hurricane track observation with time and spatial differences (and wind change) relative to the previous observation for the same storm (sid).
params.when_to_use: Compute per-observation change rates (speed proxy in degrees/sec) for individual storm tracks | Measure displacement or heading approximations between consecutive track points for a storm | Detect rapid intensification or weakening by comparing consecutive usa_wind values | Compose into time-series analyses of storm motion or intensity by joining to storm-level metadata | Filter or flag observations that represent large jumps in position, time gaps, or sudden wind changes
params.output_schema: sid: storm identifier from base table `hurricanes.sid`. Primary partition key used to compute deltas. | season: storm season from base table `hurricanes.season` (year). | number: storm number from base table `hurricanes.number` (seasonal index or identifier). | iso_time: observation timestamp from base table `hurricanes.iso_time` (current row). | latitude: canonical observation latitude from base table `hurricanes.latitude` (current row). | longitude: canonical observation longitude from base table `hurricanes.longitude` (current row). | usa_latitude: reporting-agency (USA) latitude from base table `hurricanes.usa_latitude` (current row), if present. | usa_longitude: reporting-agency (USA) longitude from base table `hurricanes.usa_longitude` (current row), if present. | usa_wind: reporting-agency (USA) wind speed from base table `hurricanes.usa_wind` (current row). | prev_iso_time: iso_time of the previous observation for the same sid (computed with LAG over PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time). | seconds_since_prev: TIMESTAMP_DIFF(iso_time, prev_iso_time, SECOND) — seconds elapsed since the previous observation for the same sid. | delta_lat_deg: latitude - prev_latitude (difference in degrees latitude vs previous observation). | delta_lon_deg: longitude - prev_longitude (difference in degrees longitude vs previous observation). | delta_usa_wind: usa_wind - prev_usa_wind (change in reported wind vs previous observation). | deg_per_second: sqrt(delta_lat_deg^2 + delta_lon_deg^2) / seconds_since_prev computed with SAFE_DIVIDE and NULLIF to avoid divide-by-zero; units = degrees of lat/lon per second (not geodesic).
params.metric: prev_iso_time = LAG(iso_time) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) | seconds_since_prev = TIMESTAMP_DIFF(iso_time, prev_iso_time, SECOND) | delta_lat_deg = latitude - LAG(latitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) | delta_lon_deg = longitude - LAG(longitude) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) | delta_usa_wind = usa_wind - LAG(usa_wind) OVER (PARTITION BY sid ORDER BY iso_time) | deg_per_second = SAFE_DIVIDE( SQRT( POW(delta_lat_deg, 2) + POW(delta_lon_deg, 2) ), NULLIF(seconds_since_prev, 0) )
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to storm-level or one-row-per-sid views/dimensions (e.g., a hypothetical storm metadata view keyed by sid or by (season, number)) on sid — safe because storm_observation_deltas_win is one row per observation (sid+iso_time) and the join target is one-row-per-sid, so each observation remains one row and measures are not duplicated. | You may join to a one-row-per-(sid,iso_time) upstream view/table on (sid, iso_time) — safe because keys align exactly, preserving row cardinality. | Do NOT join directly to any one-to-many table or view keyed only by sid or (season,number) that contains multiple rows per sid (for example: a table of multiple station reports, multiple observations buckets, or any aggregation partition that produces multiple rows per sid) without first aggregating that table to one row per sid or per (sid,iso_time) as appropriate — such joins will multiply rows and duplicate/overcount the deltas and deg_per_second measures. | Do NOT join to sibling WIN/SET/AGG/RANK views that are many-per-sid (e.g., a per-storm ranked list or per-box aggregates) unless you aggregate their rows to the same grain (sid+iso_time or sid) before joining; if you need to attach many child rows, perform an explicit aggregation (e.g., AVG, MAX) of the child measures to one value per sid or per (sid,iso_time) to avoid measure duplication. | When composing time-series aggregations from this view (e.g., average deg_per_second per storm or per day), aggregate deg_per_second or seconds_since_prev after joining any additional dimensions — do not rely on row counts to normalize rates unless the join keys are cardinality-safe as described above. | If you need geographic distance in meters/nautical miles, compute geodesic distance externally from delta_lat_deg and delta_lon_deg (this view exposes raw degree differences intentionally); converting to true speed requires converting degree-based displacement to distance using an appropriate projection or haversine formula before dividing by seconds_since_prev.

storm_observation_deltas_win.description: Compute lead/lag differences in time, position and wind within each storm to support translation speed, displacement, and intensification rate calculations. Useful for time-series analyses and estimating storm motion between consecutive observations. | Use for: Estimate storm translation speed or displacement between observations; Compute intensification rates (wind change per time); Filter rapid intensification events by delta_usa_wind and seconds_since_prev

seasonal_storm_summary_agg.name: seasonal_storm_summary_agg
seasonal_storm_summary_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid,
  season,
  name,
  basin,
  MIN(iso_time) AS first_obs_time,
  MAX(iso_time) AS last_obs_time,
  COUNT(1) AS obs_count,
  MAX(usa_wind) AS max_usa_wind,
  MAX(wmo_wind) AS max_wmo_wind,
  MIN(usa_pressure) AS min_usa_pressure,
  MIN(wmo_pressure) AS min_wmo_pressure,
  AVG(usa_wind) AS avg_usa_wind,
  AVG(wmo_wind) AS avg_wmo_wind,
  AVG(dist2land) AS avg_dist2land,
  SUM(CASE WHEN landfall = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS landfall_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
GROUP BY
  sid, season, name, basin

params.description: Per-storm (sid, season, name, basin) summary aggregations of observations: timing, counts, extreme and average intensity measures, mean distance-to-land, and a landfall count.
params.when_to_use: Get start/end times, observation counts, peak and mean wind/pressure values, and landfall counts for a specific storm or set of storms. | Rank or compare storms by peak or average intensity (e.g., max wind, min pressure) at the storm-level. | Filter storms by season, basin, or name and retrieve storm-level summary measures for reporting or downstream joins. | Serve as an aggregated base when composing further storm-level analytics (e.g., join to storm-level metadata, impact tables, or rankings).
params.output_schema: sid: storm identifier — directly forwarded from hurricanes.sid | season: storm season/year — directly forwarded from hurricanes.season | name: storm name — directly forwarded from hurricanes.name | basin: basin code where storm occurred — directly forwarded from hurricanes.basin | first_obs_time: earliest observation time for this storm (MIN(iso_time)) — derived from hurricanes.iso_time | last_obs_time: latest observation time for this storm (MAX(iso_time)) — derived from hurricanes.iso_time | obs_count: number of observations rows aggregated for this storm (COUNT(1)) — count of rows in hurricanes for the group | max_usa_wind: maximum usa_wind value observed for this storm (MAX(usa_wind)) — derived from hurricanes.usa_wind | max_wmo_wind: maximum wmo_wind value observed for this storm (MAX(wmo_wind)) — derived from hurricanes.wmo_wind | min_usa_pressure: minimum usa_pressure observed for this storm (MIN(usa_pressure)) — derived from hurricanes.usa_pressure | min_wmo_pressure: minimum wmo_pressure observed for this storm (MIN(wmo_pressure)) — derived from hurricanes.wmo_pressure | avg_usa_wind: arithmetic mean of usa_wind across observations for this storm (AVG(usa_wind)) — derived from hurricanes.usa_wind | avg_wmo_wind: arithmetic mean of wmo_wind across observations for this storm (AVG(wmo_wind)) — derived from hurricanes.wmo_wind | avg_dist2land: arithmetic mean of dist2land across observations for this storm (AVG(dist2land)) — derived from hurricanes.dist2land | landfall_count: sum of indicator for landfall events (SUM(CASE WHEN landfall = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) — counts rows where hurricanes.landfall = 0
params.metric: first_obs_time = MIN(bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.iso_time) | last_obs_time = MAX(bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.iso_time) | obs_count = COUNT(1) over group (sid, season, name, basin) | max_usa_wind = MAX(bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.usa_wind) | max_wmo_wind = MAX(bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.wmo_wind) | min_usa_pressure = MIN(bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.usa_pressure) | min_wmo_pressure = MIN(bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.wmo_pressure) | avg_usa_wind = AVG(bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.usa_wind) | avg_wmo_wind = AVG(bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.wmo_wind) | avg_dist2land = AVG(bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.dist2land) | landfall_count = SUM(CASE WHEN bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.landfall = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to storm-level (one-row-per-storm) dimensions or views on (sid, season, name, basin) — safe because this view is one-row-per (sid, season, name, basin) and so its aggregated measures will not be duplicated. Example safe join: join to a storm metadata dimension that has primary key (sid, season, name, basin). | do NOT join directly to one-to-many observation-level tables (including the original hurricanes table or any normalized observation view) on (sid, season, name, basin) without re-aggregation — such joins will multiply rows and thus over-count obs_count, sums, and distort averages/min/max. If you must combine with observation-level rows, either (a) re-aggregate the observation table to the same storm grain before joining, or (b) join using a subquery that aggregates to storm-level first. | do NOT join to other one-to-many event/detail tables (e.g., per-observation reports) without aggregating them to storm-level; instead compute metrics on those tables grouped by (sid, season, name, basin) and then join storm-level-to-storm-level. | If joining to ranking or windowed sibling views that are also one-row-per-storm (e.g., storm_peak_intensity_rank) join on (sid, season, name, basin) — safe because both sides are storm-grain. | When composing further aggregations that combine this view's measures with measures from other grains, treat this view as an atomic storm-level input (one row per storm). To produce correct higher-level aggregates (season-level, basin-level), SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX over the storm rows in this view rather than joining back to lower-grain detail.

seasonal_storm_summary_agg.description: Aggregated measures per storm (sid) and season: counts of observations, maximum/minimum/mean of key intensity measures and earliest/latest observation times. Useful for season-level rollups and identifying storm-level maxima for further ranking. | Use for: List storms with highest maximum wind in a season; Compute storms with most observations or longest duration; Count landfalls per storm or season

grain: sid, iso_time, agency -- one row per original observation per agency columnset

params.description: Provides a long (unpivoted) listing of hurricane observations for each reporting agency (wmo, usa, tokyo, cma, reunion) so you can analyze per-agency position and intensity at each observation time.
params.when_to_use: When you need one row per original hurricane observation per reporting agency (e.g., compare agency-reported wind/pressure/position over time). | When composing additional filters, aggregations or joins keyed at the observation (sid, iso_time) and agency level (for example: compute average agency wind by storm or time window). | When joining meteorological measures to spatial or storm-level dimensions (e.g., map agency positions or attach storm metadata) without duplicating agency-specific measures.
params.output_schema: sid: storm identifier (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.sid) | season: hurricane season / year (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.season) | number: storm number within the season (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.number) | name: storm name (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.name) | iso_time: observation timestamp in ISO format (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes.iso_time) | agency: reporting agency code; one of 'wmo','usa','tokyo','cma','reunion' (derived literal in each UNION branch) | ag_latitude: agency-reported latitude for the observation (from respective base column: latitude, usa_latitude, tokyo_latitude, cma_latitude, reunion_latitude) | ag_longitude: agency-reported longitude for the observation (from respective base column: longitude, usa_longitude, tokyo_longitude, cma_longitude, reunion_longitude) | ag_wind: agency-reported wind speed for the observation (from respective base column: wmo_wind, usa_wind, tokyo_wind, cma_wind, reunion_wind) | ag_pressure: agency-reported pressure for the observation (from respective base column: wmo_pressure, usa_pressure, tokyo_pressure, cma_pressure, reunion_pressure)
params.metric: ag_wind = direct pass-through of the agency-specific wind column (no aggregation). Possible values come from: wmo_wind, usa_wind, tokyo_wind, cma_wind, reunion_wind depending on agency. | ag_pressure = direct pass-through of the agency-specific pressure column (no aggregation). Possible values come from: wmo_pressure, usa_pressure, tokyo_pressure, cma_pressure, reunion_pressure depending on agency.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to storm-level or observation-dimension tables on (sid, iso_time) — safe because this view is one row per (sid, iso_time, agency). Example: JOIN storm_observation_metadata USING (sid, iso_time) will not duplicate ag_wind/ag_pressure because the view already has at most one row per agency per observation. | You can safely join to a storm-level dim keyed by sid (e.g., seasonal_storm_summary_agg on sid) because the view is at (sid, iso_time, agency) and the dim is one-row-per-sid; measures in this view will not be duplicated when joining on sid alone. | Do NOT join this view directly to any one-to-many table keyed only by (sid, iso_time) or (sid) that contains multiple rows per observation (for example: a table of multiple sensor reports, track segments, or other per-observation breakdowns) without re-aggregating first. Such joins will multiply rows and thus duplicate ag_wind/ag_pressure counts or sums. If you need combined results, either: | - aggregate this view upward to the join key before joining (e.g., GROUP BY sid, iso_time to produce a single row per observation/agency), or | - join on the full key (sid, iso_time, agency) to maintain 1:1 relation when the other table is also at agency granularity. | When joining to sibling normalized views: ensure keys include agency when the sibling contains agency-specific rows (if any). If the sibling is storm-level normalized (one row per sid), joining on sid is safe; if the sibling is a per-time series (one-to-many per iso_time), re-aggregate one side first.

agency_measure_unpivot_reshape.description: Unpivot key per-agency intensity measurements (latitude, longitude, wind, pressure) into rows with an 'agency' column and normalized measure columns. Useful when comparing or aggregating across agencies or when you need a long form of agency-specific observations. | Use for: Compare wind/pressure reported by different agencies at the same time; Aggregate agency-specific statistics across storms or seasons; Select observations for a particular agency in long form

icoads_core_events_sel.name: icoads_core_events_sel
icoads_core_events_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  year,
  month,
  day,
  hour,
  TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(CAST((UNIX_SECONDS(TIMESTAMP(CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING),'-',LPAD(CAST(month AS STRING),2,'0'),'-',LPAD(CAST(day AS STRING),2,'0'),' ', '00:00:00'))) + CAST(FLOOR(hour) AS INT64)*3600) AS INT64)), HOUR) AS obs_hour_truncated,
  -- keep raw coords and precision indicator
  latitude,
  longitude,
  latlong_indicator,
  -- identifiers
  callsign,
  country_code,
  deck,
  id_indicator,
  national_source_indicator,
  -- scaled numeric measures (convert stored scaled units to human units where documented)
  wind_speed AS wind_speed_tenths_m_s,
  CASE WHEN wind_speed IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) END AS wind_speed_m_s,
  sea_level_pressure AS sea_level_pressure_tenths_hpa,
  CASE WHEN sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) END AS sea_level_pressure_hpa,
  amt_pressure_tend AS amt_pressure_tend_tenths_hpa,
  CASE WHEN amt_pressure_tend IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(amt_pressure_tend, 10.0) END AS amt_pressure_tend_hpa,
  air_temperature AS air_temperature_c,
  wetbulb_temperature AS wetbulb_temperature_c,
  dewpoint_temperature AS dewpoint_temperature_c,
  sea_surface_temp AS sea_surface_temp_tenths_c,
  CASE WHEN sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp,10.0) END AS sea_surface_temp_c,
  wave_height,
  swell_height,
  -- key categorical codes preserved for decoding later
  wind_direction_true,
  wind_direction_indicator,
  wind_speed_indicator,
  visibility,
  visibility_indicator,
  present_weather,
  past_weather,
  sst_measurement_method,
  total_cloud_amount,
  lower_cloud_amount,
  low_cloud_type,
  middle_cloud_type,
  high_cloud_type,
  cloud_height_indicator,
  cloud_height,
  ten_degree_box_number,
  one_degree_box_number,
  attm_count,
  imma_version
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
WHERE
  TRUE
grain: one row per original icoads observation record (as in underlying shards)

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: use to restrict years (e.g., BETWEEN '2005' AND '2017')
semantic_filters.latitude/longitude: use bounding predicates for geographic subsets
semantic_filters.callsign/country_code: filter by reporting platform or recruiting country

icoads_core_events_sel.description: Select and project core observation fields with assembled observation_date and standard scaled measures. Use this to filter observations by year (_TABLE_SUFFIX), geographic box, callsign, country, or other predicates. Preserves identifiers and key measures for downstream joins/aggregations. | Use for: Filter observations by year range and region; compute basic stats per box or per callsign; feed into aggregations for monthly/yearly summaries

icoads_monthly_agg_per_box.name: icoads_monthly_agg_per_box
icoads_monthly_agg_per_box.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  year,
  month,
  CAST(FLOOR((latitude + 90) / 10) AS INT64) AS ten_degree_box_number,
  CAST(FLOOR((latitude + 90) )*360 + CAST(FLOOR((longitude + 180)) AS INT64) AS INT64) AS one_degree_box_number,
  COUNT(1) AS obs_count,
  COUNTIF(wind_speed IS NOT NULL) AS cnt_wind_speed,
  AVG(CASE WHEN wind_speed IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) END) AS avg_wind_speed_m_s,
  MIN(CASE WHEN wind_speed IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) END) AS min_wind_speed_m_s,
  MAX(CASE WHEN wind_speed IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) END) AS max_wind_speed_m_s,
  COUNTIF(sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL) AS cnt_sst,
  AVG(CASE WHEN sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) END) AS avg_sst_c,
  MIN(CASE WHEN sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) END) AS min_sst_c,
  MAX(CASE WHEN sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) END) AS max_sst_c,
  COUNTIF(sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL) AS cnt_sea_level_pressure,
  AVG(CASE WHEN sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) END) AS avg_sea_level_pressure_hpa,
  MIN(CASE WHEN sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) END) AS min_sea_level_pressure_hpa,
  MAX(CASE WHEN sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) END) AS max_sea_level_pressure_hpa
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2005' AND '2017'
GROUP BY
  table_suffix,
  year,
  month,
  ten_degree_box_number,
  one_degree_box_number

SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) END) — maximum sea_surface_temp in °C | cnt_sea_level_pressure: COUNTIF(sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL) — number of observations with non-null sea_level_pressure | sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) END) — maximum sea_level_pressure in hPa

params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimension or lookup that is 1-row-per-(ten_degree_box_number) or 1-row-per-(one_degree_box_number) on the matching box key — safe because this view already has at most one row per (table_suffix, year, month, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number) and joining to a one-row-per-box table will not multiply measure rows. Example: join to a spatial_box_lookup on one_degree_box_number or ten_degree_box_number. | Do NOT join directly to any one-to-many detail table (e.g., raw observation tables, station-level tables with many stations per box, or any view that is at finer grain) without first aggregating that table up to the view's grain (table_suffix, year, month, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number). Such joins would multiply this view's measures because this AGG is already aggregated; if you need combined metrics, re-aggregate after the join or join on keys that guarantee one-to-one. | If you need to combine with station or event dimensions (e.g., stations_dim or icoads_core_sel_basic_obs), ensure you join on a unique key present in that dimension (one-to-one) or aggregate the dimension side to the same monthly-box grain before joining. For example, safe: AGG JOIN stations_dim ON stations_dim.ten_degree_box_number = AGG.ten_degree_box_number only if stations_dim has been reduced to one row per ten_degree_box_number (otherwise it's many-to-one and will duplicate counts). | When joining to other aggregate views in the same DB: joining to another view aggregated to the same grouping keys (table_suffix, year, month, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number) is safe and will not duplicate metrics. Joining to views aggregated at a coarser grain (e.g., year-only or table_suffix+year) is allowed but requires grouping/aggregation after the join to produce correct combined metrics. | If you must join to a one-to-many relation and preserve AGG's metrics, use keyed aggregation patterns: either (a) aggregate the many-side to the AGG grain first, or (b) compute desired derived measures from AGG only and do not SUM/AVG AGG columns across duplicated rows without dividing by the duplication factor.

icoads_top_observations_rank.name: icoads_top_observations_rank
icoads_top_observations_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  month,
  ten_degree_box_number,
  one_degree_box_number,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  callsign,
  deck,
  wind_speed AS wind_speed_tenths_m_s,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) AS wind_speed_m_s,
  sea_surface_temp AS sea_surface_temp_tenths_c,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) AS sea_surface_temp_c,
  sea_level_pressure AS sea_level_pressure_tenths_hpa,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) AS sea_level_pressure_hpa,
  -- rank highest wind_speed within year + ten_degree_box_number partition
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_wind_speed_desc,
  -- rank highest SST within year + ten_degree_box_number partition
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_sst_desc,
  -- rank lowest sea level pressure within year + ten_degree_box_number partition
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) ASC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_slp_asc
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000`
grain: one row per original observation with ranks assigned within year + ten_degree_box_number partitions

params.description: Provides one-row-per-original-ICoads observation with ranks (within each year and 10-degree ocean box) for wind speed (high to low), sea surface temperature (high to low), and sea level pressure (low to high), plus original observation fields and converted metric units.
params.when_to_use: Find the top (highest) wind speed observations within each year and ten_degree_box_number (e.g., top N per box-year). | Find the top (highest) sea surface temperature observations within each year and ten_degree_box_number. | Find the lowest sea level pressure observations within each year and ten_degree_box_number. | Filter or join individual observations that are top-ranked by wind, SST, or SLP and then inspect their location/callsign/deck/time (year/month). | Compose further aggregations (e.g., count of top-1 observations per station or per box) by grouping on the view's identifying columns and rank columns. | Serve as a base for dashboards or downstream queries that need original observation rows augmented with within-box-year ranks and metric-unit conversions.
params.output_schema: year: observation year (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.year) | month: observation month (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.month) | ten_degree_box_number: 10-degree spatial box identifier (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.ten_degree_box_number) | one_degree_box_number: 1-degree spatial box identifier (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.one_degree_box_number) | latitude: observation latitude in original source units (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.latitude) | longitude: observation longitude in original source units (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.longitude) | callsign: ship/station callsign identifier (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.callsign) | deck: data deck/source identifier (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.deck) | wind_speed_tenths_m_s: wind_speed as stored in source (integer/units: tenths of m/s) (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.wind_speed) | wind_speed_m_s: wind_speed in m/s (computed as SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0)) | sea_surface_temp_tenths_c: sea_surface_temp as stored in source (integer/units: tenths of °C) (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.sea_surface_temp) | sea_surface_temp_c: sea_surface_temp in °C (computed as SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0)) | sea_level_pressure_tenths_hpa: sea_level_pressure as stored in source (integer/units: tenths of hPa) (from bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.sea_level_pressure) | sea_level_pressure_hpa: sea_level_pressure in hPa (computed as SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0)) | rank_by_wind_speed_desc: integer rank for wind speed within (year, ten_degree_box_number), 1 = highest wind_speed_m_s; ties receive same rank (RANK window function). | rank_by_sst_desc: integer rank for sea_surface_temp within (year, ten_degree_box_number), 1 = highest sea_surface_temp_c; ties receive same rank. | rank_by_slp_asc: integer rank for sea_level_pressure within (year, ten_degree_box_number), 1 = lowest sea_level_pressure_hpa; ties receive same rank.
params.metric: wind_speed_m_s = SAFE_DIVIDE(bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.wind_speed, 10.0) | sea_surface_temp_c = SAFE_DIVIDE(bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.sea_surface_temp, 10.0) | sea_level_pressure_hpa = SAFE_DIVIDE(bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_1662_2000.sea_level_pressure, 10.0) | rank_by_wind_speed_desc = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(wind_speed, 10.0) DESC NULLS LAST) | rank_by_sst_desc = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_surface_temp, 10.0) DESC NULLS LAST) | rank_by_slp_asc = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, ten_degree_box_number ORDER BY SAFE_DIVIDE(sea_level_pressure, 10.0) ASC NULLS LAST)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/lookups that are one-row-per-key using keys present in this view — safe examples: |   - join to stations_dim on callsign (join to stations_dim.callsign = icoads_top_observations_rank.callsign) — safe if stations_dim is one-row-per-callsign because this view is one-row-per-original-observation (joining a 1:N dim will not duplicate this view's rows, but joining a 1:1 dim preserves row-level identity). |   - join to any per-box/year aggregated view on (year, ten_degree_box_number) if that view is aggregated to the same grain (one-row-per-year-ten_degree_box) — safe because both sides are at compatible grains and will not multiply measures. |  | do NOT join without care (will multiply rows/measures) to these one-to-many/detail tables or windowed/sequence views unless you re-aggregate after the join: |   - do NOT directly join to icoads_obs_by_callsign_sequences_win or ship_observation_sequences_win or other WIN/SEQUENCE views that produce multiple rows per original observation (they are one-to-many relative to this view) without aggregating, because those joins will duplicate this view's measures and ranks. |   - do NOT join to event/detail tables that have multiple rows per observation (for example, event reports or unpivoted measure reshapes) without grouping/aggregating first, since each matching detail row would multiply original-observation rows. |  | recommended composition patterns: |   - Filtering/selection: query this view and filter on rank_by_* columns (e.g., WHERE rank_by_wind_speed_desc = 1) to get top obs per box-year; then join to stations_dim (1:1) for station metadata. |   - Aggregation after join: if you must join to a one-to-many table (e.g., measures unpivot/reshaped tables), perform the join within a subquery and then re-aggregate (GROUP BY the view's primary identifying columns such as year, month, ten_degree_box_number, one_degree_box_number, latitude, longitude, callsign, deck) to restore one-row-per-original-observation before using ranks as stable measures. |   - Grouping on ranks: when computing counts of top-ranked observations per station/box, GROUP BY icoads_top_observations_rank.callsign or ten_degree_box_number and use COUNT(*) filtered by rank conditions; these aggregations are safe and preferable to joins that would duplicate rows.

icoads_observation_counts_by_country.name: icoads_observation_counts_by_country
icoads_observation_counts_by_country.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS table_suffix,
  year,
  month,
  country_code,
  COUNT(1) AS obs_count,
  COUNTIF(sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL) AS cnt_sst,
  COUNTIF(air_temperature IS NOT NULL) AS cnt_air_temperature,
  COUNTIF(wind_speed IS NOT NULL) AS cnt_wind_speed,
  COUNTIF(sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL) AS cnt_sea_level_pressure
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2005' AND '2017'
GROUP BY
  _TABLE_SUFFIX,
  year,
  month,
  country_code

semantic_filters._TABLE_SUFFIX: restrict years/shards to include relevant period

params.description: Monthly counts of ICOADS observations by source table (year-month) and reporting country, including counts of non-null measured variables (SST, air temp, wind speed, sea level pressure).
params.when_to_use: Get total observation volume per month and country within ICOADS (2005–2017) and the availability of key measured variables. | Filter or trend analyses that need per-country monthly sample sizes before computing rates or averages (e.g., compute percent of obs with SST). | As an aggregated building block to join with country or time dimensions (one row per table_suffix-year-month-country) when composing higher-level aggregates (annual, regional) without re-scanning raw ICOADS tables.
params.output_schema: table_suffix: source table suffix string derived from _TABLE_SUFFIX in the underlying wildcard table (bigquery-public-data.noaa_icoads.icoads_core_*). | year: reporting year (integer) from the base table column year. | month: reporting month (integer) from the base table column month. | country_code: reporting country code (string) from the base table column country_code. | obs_count: total number of observations in that (table_suffix, year, month, country_code) group; derived as COUNT(1) over the grouped ICOADS rows. | cnt_sst: count of rows in the group where sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL; derived from COUNTIF(sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL). | cnt_air_temperature: count of rows in the group where air_temperature IS NOT NULL; derived from COUNTIF(air_temperature IS NOT NULL). | cnt_wind_speed: count of rows in the group where wind_speed IS NOT NULL; derived from COUNTIF(wind_speed IS NOT NULL). | cnt_sea_level_pressure: count of rows in the group where sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL; derived from COUNTIF(sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL).
params.metric: obs_count = COUNT(1)  -- count of raw ICOADS rows per (table_suffix, year, month, country_code) | cnt_sst = COUNTIF(sea_surface_temp IS NOT NULL)  -- number of rows with non-null sea_surface_temp in the group | cnt_air_temperature = COUNTIF(air_temperature IS NOT NULL)  -- number of rows with non-null air_temperature in the group | cnt_wind_speed = COUNTIF(wind_speed IS NOT NULL)  -- number of rows with non-null wind_speed in the group | cnt_sea_level_pressure = COUNTIF(sea_level_pressure IS NOT NULL)  -- number of rows with non-null sea_level_pressure in the group
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to country dimension tables (e.g., a countries dim keyed by country_code) ON country_code — safe because this view is one row per (table_suffix, year, month, country_code), so joining a 1-row-per-country dimension will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a time dimension keyed by (year, month) or (table_suffix, year, month) — safe because the time dim is 1-to-1 for the time grain used by this view. | unsafe join warning: do NOT join directly to any table or view that is one-to-many at the (table_suffix, year, month, country_code) grain (for example: a raw observations table, station-level tables with multiple stations per country-month, or any event/observation-level view) without first aggregating that table to the same grain. Such joins will multiply obs_count and the other counts and produce incorrect totals. | unsafe join warning: when joining to sibling aggregated views that have a different grain (e.g., aggregated by box, station, or daily instead of monthly-country), either aggregate those siblings to (table_suffix, year, month, country_code) or join at coarser grain with care and re-aggregate after the join. | composition tip: to compute derived rates (e.g., pct_sst = cnt_sst / obs_count), compute the expression using this view's columns directly. To combine with other measures coming from one-to-many dimensions, perform aggregation after joining (e.g., SUM(obs_count) grouped by desired keys) to avoid duplication. | example safe pattern: SELECT s.country_name, SUM(v.obs_count) AS total_obs FROM icoads_observation_counts_by_country v JOIN countries_dim s ON v.country_code = s.iso_code GROUP BY s.country_name; — safe because countries_dim is 1 row per country. | example unsafe pattern: SELECT v.*, st.station_name FROM icoads_observation_counts_by_country v JOIN stations_dim st ON v.country_code = st.country_code; — unsafe if stations_dim has multiple stations per country because station rows will duplicate v's counts; remedy: aggregate stations_dim to 1 row per country before joining or join only to a station-level metric that has been pre-aggregated to the view's grain.
