Use this when filtering events by time, location, magnitude, or impact measures. | Use for: Filter events by year/month/day or timestamp range; Select events by country, region_code or geographic bounding box; Use magnitude or impact measures for cohort selection; Prepare events for joins to spatial lookups or time-series analysis

earthquakes_magnitudes_unpivot.name: earthquakes_magnitudes_unpivot
earthquakes_magnitudes_unpivot.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  year,
  month,
  day,
  event_ts AS event_timestamp_utc,
  magnitude_type,
  magnitude_value
FROM (
  SELECT
    id,
    year,
    month,
    day,
    SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(month,1) AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(day,1) AS STRING),2,'0'))) AS event_ts,
    eq_mag_mw,
    eq_mag_ms,
    eq_mag_mb,
    eq_mag_ml,
    eq_mag_mfa,
    eq_mag_unk,
    eq_primary
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes`
)
UNPIVOT (
  magnitude_value FOR magnitude_type IN (eq_mag_mw AS 'MW', eq_mag_ms AS 'MS', eq_mag_mb AS 'MB', eq_mag_ml AS 'ML', eq_mag_mfa AS 'MFA', eq_mag_unk AS 'UNK', eq_primary AS 'PRIMARY')
)
WHERE magnitude_value IS NOT NULL
grain: id, magnitude_type -- one row per event per available magnitude type

params.description: A reshaped/unpivoted view that returns one row per earthquake event id and magnitude type, with the event date/timestamp and the reported magnitude value and its type.
params.when_to_use: List or filter earthquake magnitudes by event and magnitude type (e.g., show all MW magnitudes or compare MW vs ML for events). | Aggregate magnitudes across events by type (e.g., average MW per year) — use this view as the measure source and then GROUP BY magnitude_type. | Join earthquake magnitudes to event-level metadata (location, impact) when you need one row per event-magnitude combination. | Build time-series or seasonal analyses of magnitudes (year/month/day) where magnitude values are the metric of interest. | Normalize downstream queries so they don't need UNPIVOT logic — useful when composing across different magnitude columns uniformly.
params.output_schema: id: earthquake event identifier from base table (`bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.id`) | year: event year from base table (`...earthquakes.year`) | month: event month from base table (`...earthquakes.month`) — may be NULL in source and COALESCE'd to 1 when building event_timestamp_utc, but the output month column is the original month value | day: event day from base table (`...earthquakes.day`) — may be NULL in source and COALESCE'd to 1 when building event_timestamp_utc, but the output day column is the original day value | event_timestamp_utc: derived TIMESTAMP parsed from year, month, day using SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(year,'-',LPAD(COALESCE(month,1),2,'0'),'-',LPAD(COALESCE(day,1),2,'0'))) — represents a best-effort UTC date for the event constructed from year/month/day | magnitude_type: the magnitude column name mapped to a short code (one of 'MW','MS','MB','ML','MFA','UNK','PRIMARY') produced by the UNPIVOT expression (derived from the column aliases in the UNPIVOT clause) | magnitude_value: numeric magnitude value taken from the corresponding magnitude column (eq_mag_mw, eq_mag_ms, eq_mag_mb, eq_mag_ml, eq_mag_mfa, eq_mag_unk, eq_primary) — only non-NULL magnitudes are included
params.metric: magnitude_value = direct value from one of the source magnitude columns (eq_mag_mw | eq_mag_ms | eq_mag_mb | eq_mag_ml | eq_mag_mfa | eq_mag_unk | eq_primary) — this is not an aggregate, it's a reshaped scalar measure per (id, magnitude_type) | event_timestamp_utc = SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d', CONCAT(CAST(year AS STRING), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(month,1) AS STRING),2,'0'), '-', LPAD(CAST(COALESCE(day,1) AS STRING),2,'0')))
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to event-level dimension tables (for example, any events_core / earthquakes_core_events_sel-like view keyed by id) on id — safe because this view is one row per (id, magnitude_type) so joining by id does NOT duplicate magnitude_value per (id, magnitude_type) if the target is strictly one row per id (one-to-one or many-to-one from this view to the dimension). | You may aggregate this view to event-level (GROUP BY id) before joining to one-to-many tables to avoid duplication. Example safe pattern: first compute event-level metrics like MAX(magnitude_value) FILTER(WHERE magnitude_type='MW') by grouping on id, then join to a one-to-many table. | Do NOT join this view directly to other tables/views that are one-to-many relative to (id, magnitude_type) (for example, event reports or many observation rows per event) without re-aggregating either side — such joins will multiply rows and therefore multiply magnitude_value occurrences, producing incorrect totals/averages. | When composing with sibling RESHAPE/UNPIVOT views (e.g., tsunami_events_magnitude_unpivot or icoads_measures_unpivot_reshape), join on (id, magnitude_type) only if both are at the same grain and represent the same kind of measure; otherwise prefer joining on id and keeping magnitude_type separate or aggregating by id first. | When aggregating across magnitude_type, use explicit grouping by magnitude_type to preserve correct measure semantics (e.g., AVG(magnitude_value) GROUP BY magnitude_type). | If you need event_timestamp_utc as a strict point-in-time key for joins, be aware it is constructed from year/month/day (month/day may be NULL in source and are coerced to 1 when parsing); verify this behavior if exact original timestamps are required.

earthquakes_magnitudes_unpivot.description: Unpivot the multiple magnitude columns into a canonical (magnitude_type, magnitude_value) pair per event. Use this when you need to compare magnitudes across scales or rank events by any magnitude type. | Use for: Rank or filter events by magnitude across different magnitude scales; Compare primary magnitude vs alternative magnitude scales; Aggregate event counts above magnitude thresholds irrespective of scale by choosing a magnitude_type

earthquakes_impact_agg_by_year_country.name: earthquakes_impact_agg_by_year_country
earthquakes_impact_agg_by_year_country.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  country,
  COUNT(1) AS events_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(deaths,0)) AS sum_deaths,
  SUM(IFNULL(missing,0)) AS sum_missing,
  SUM(IFNULL(injuries,0)) AS sum_injuries,
  SUM(IFNULL(damage_millions_dollars,0)) AS sum_damage_millions_dollars,
  SUM(IFNULL(houses_destroyed,0)) AS sum_houses_destroyed,
  SUM(IFNULL(houses_damaged,0)) AS sum_houses_damaged,
  SUM(IFNULL(total_deaths,0)) AS sum_total_deaths,
  SUM(IFNULL(total_missing,0)) AS sum_total_missing,
  SUM(IFNULL(total_injuries,0)) AS sum_total_injuries,
  SUM(IFNULL(total_damage_millions_dollars,0)) AS sum_total_damage_millions_dollars,
  SUM(IFNULL(total_houses_destroyed,0)) AS sum_total_houses_destroyed
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes`
GROUP BY
  year,
  country

params.description: Annual per-country aggregates of earthquake event counts and summed impact measures (deaths, missing, injuries, damage in millions, houses destroyed/damaged, and their 'total_' counterparts).
params.when_to_use: Count earthquakes and sum human/property impacts by year and country (reporting, dashboards). | Trend analysis over years for a specific country (time series of annual totals). | Comparing annual impact totals between countries (ranking, share calculations). | As an aggregated building block to join to country or year dimension tables for labeling or to compute rates per population (when joined safely — see composition). | Do not use this view to compute event-level analyses or to drill down to individual earthquake records (it is aggregated to year+country).
params.output_schema: year: calendar year of the earthquake event grouping (derived from earthquakes.year) | country: country name or country code value as stored in the earthquakes table (derived from earthquakes.country) | events_count: number of earthquake events in that year and country (COUNT(1) from earthquakes rows that share the year+country) | sum_deaths: SUM(IFNULL(deaths,0)) — sum of the earthquakes.deaths column for events in the group | sum_missing: SUM(IFNULL(missing,0)) — sum of the earthquakes.missing column for events in the group | sum_injuries: SUM(IFNULL(injuries,0)) — sum of the earthquakes.injuries column for events in the group | sum_damage_millions_dollars: SUM(IFNULL(damage_millions_dollars,0)) — sum of earthquakes.damage_millions_dollars in the group | sum_houses_destroyed: SUM(IFNULL(houses_destroyed,0)) — sum of earthquakes.houses_destroyed in the group | sum_houses_damaged: SUM(IFNULL(houses_damaged,0)) — sum of earthquakes.houses_damaged in the group | sum_total_deaths: SUM(IFNULL(total_deaths,0)) — sum of earthquakes.total_deaths in the group | sum_total_missing: SUM(IFNULL(total_missing,0)) — sum of earthquakes.total_missing in the group | sum_total_injuries: SUM(IFNULL(total_injuries,0)) — sum of earthquakes.total_injuries in the group | sum_total_damage_millions_dollars: SUM(IFNULL(total_damage_millions_dollars,0)) — sum of earthquakes.total_damage_millions_dollars in the group | sum_total_houses_destroyed: SUM(IFNULL(total_houses_destroyed,0)) — sum of earthquakes.total_houses_destroyed in the group
params.metric: events_count = COUNT(1) over rows in earthquakes grouped by (year, country) | sum_deaths = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.deaths, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_missing = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.missing, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_injuries = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.injuries, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_damage_millions_dollars = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.damage_millions_dollars, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_houses_destroyed = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.houses_destroyed, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_houses_damaged = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.houses_damaged, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_total_deaths = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.total_deaths, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_total_missing = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.total_missing, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_total_injuries = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.total_injuries, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_total_damage_millions_dollars = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.total_damage_millions_dollars, 0)) grouped by (year, country) | sum_total_houses_destroyed = SUM(IFNULL(earthquakes.total_houses_destroyed, 0)) grouped by (year, country)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a country dimension (e.g., a countries lookup view/table) on this view.country = countries.country (or matching country code) — safe because this AGG has one row per (year,country); joining to a one-row-per-country dimension adds attributes without duplicating summed measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a year/calendar dimension on this view.year = calendar.year — safe for the same reason: calendar dimension is one-row-per-year and will not duplicate aggregates. | do NOT join directly to event-level or other one-to-many tables (for example, the underlying earthquakes table or any event-detail view) without re-aggregating after the join, because those joins will expand rows per aggregated key and multiply the aggregated measures (events_count and all sums). If you need to enrich by event-level attributes, join the AGG to a deduplicated or aggregated result keyed by (year,country) or re-aggregate measures after the join. | do NOT join to other aggregated views that are one-to-many relative to (year,country) (for example, a view that has multiple rows per country per year such as region-subdivision aggregations) unless you first aggregate that view to one row per (year,country) or perform a proper GROUP BY after the join to avoid double-counting. | safe composition pattern: when combining with another aggregation that is at a different grain, either (a) aggregate the other dataset to (year,country) then join on (year,country), or (b) join first on a strictly one-row-per-dimension table (year or country) and then compute any derived rates or ratios from the joined attributes. | example safe SQL pattern: SELECT a.year, a.country, a.events_count, a.sum_deaths, pop.population, a.sum_deaths / pop.population AS deaths_per_capita FROM earthquakes_impact_agg_by_year_country a JOIN country_population_dim pop ON a.country = pop.country AND a.year = pop.year; — this is safe because country_population_dim must be one-row-per-(year,country).

earthquakes_impact_agg_by_year_country.description: Aggregate key impact measures (counts and sums) by year and country. Exposes totals and event counts for deaths, injuries, damage, and houses impacted. Use this for time-series and country-level impact summaries. | Use for: Time-series of aggregated impacts by country; Compare country-year damage or deaths; Compute rates per event or per population when joined to population data

earthquakes_rank_by_magnitude_win.name: earthquakes_rank_by_magnitude_win
earthquakes_rank_by_magnitude_win.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  year,
  country,
  location_name,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  COALESCE(eq_mag_mw, eq_primary, eq_mag_ms, eq_mag_mb, eq_mag_ml, eq_mag_mfa, eq_mag_unk) AS chosen_magnitude,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, country ORDER BY COALESCE(eq_mag_mw, eq_primary, eq_mag_ms, eq_mag_mb, eq_mag_ml, eq_mag_mfa, eq_mag_unk) DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_magnitude_desc,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year, country ORDER BY COALESCE(eq_mag_mw, eq_primary, eq_mag_ms, eq_mag_mb, eq_mag_ml, eq_mag_mfa, eq_mag_unk) DESC NULLS LAST) AS rownum_by_magnitude_desc
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes`
grain: id, year, country -- one row per event augmented with rank within (year,country)

params.description: Provides one row per earthquake event with a single chosen magnitude and two rank measures (RANK and ROW_NUMBER) computed within each (year, country) partition, ordering events by magnitude descending.
params.when_to_use: Find the largest or top-N earthquakes by magnitude within a specific year and country. | Compare an event's magnitude position relative to other events in the same year and country (e.g., "what was the largest earthquake in Japan in 2011?"). | Compose further aggregations or filters based on event rank (e.g., keep only rank = 1 per (year,country) to get top events). | Join to event-level detail tables/dimensions where one-row-per-event is required (e.g., enrich with impact or report data) while preserving event granularity.
params.output_schema: id: unique event identifier from base table `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.id` | year: event year from base table `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.year` (used as partition key for ranks) | country: event country from base table `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.country` (used as partition key for ranks) | location_name: textual location from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.location_name` (informational, one row per event) | latitude: event latitude from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.latitude` (informational) | longitude: event longitude from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.longitude` (informational) | chosen_magnitude: the selected magnitude value for ranking; COALESCE(eq_mag_mw, eq_primary, eq_mag_ms, eq_mag_mb, eq_mag_ml, eq_mag_mfa, eq_mag_unk) from the base table | rank_by_magnitude_desc: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, country ORDER BY chosen_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST) — dense ranking semantics with gaps for ties within (year,country) | rownum_by_magnitude_desc: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year, country ORDER BY chosen_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST) — unique sequential row numbers within (year,country)
params.metric: chosen_magnitude = COALESCE(eq_mag_mw, eq_primary, eq_mag_ms, eq_mag_mb, eq_mag_ml, eq_mag_mfa, eq_mag_unk) -- selects the first non-null magnitude value available for the event | rank_by_magnitude_desc = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year, country ORDER BY chosen_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST) -- rank with ties (same magnitude get same rank) within each (year,country) | rownum_by_magnitude_desc = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY year, country ORDER BY chosen_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST) -- unique position within each (year,country)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to event-level detail or dimension tables keyed by id (join to <events or event-detail view> on id) — safe because this view is strictly one row per event id, so joining on id does NOT duplicate rows/measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a year or country dimension on (year) or (country) respectively — safe because the view is one row per event and the join to a dimensional key will not multiply event rows as long as the dimension side is one row per year or per country. | do NOT blindly join to any table/view that is one-to-many from event id (for example: reports, multiple observational records, or any aggregated-by-smaller-grain view) without first aggregating those one-to-many rows to the event id level (e.g., summarize counts or sums per id) because such joins will multiply this view's rows and will therefore duplicate/overcount the rank-related measures and chosen_magnitude. | do NOT join to sibling RANK or WIN views partitioned by a different grain (e.g., views that produce multiple rows per event or per sub-event) unless you aggregate or restrict them to one row per event id; otherwise rank_by_magnitude_desc and rownum_by_magnitude_desc semantics become invalid due to row multiplication. | If you need to combine with an aggregated table (e.g., earthquakes_impact_agg_by_year_country), prefer joining on (year, country) but be aware: the impact aggregation is by (year,country) — joining it to this per-event view will repeat the aggregated impact values for every event in that (year,country). To avoid duplication, either (A) aggregate the per-event measures after the join dividing/weighting appropriately, or (B) join the aggregated impact table to a pre-aggregated subset of this view (for example, restrict this view to rank = 1 per (year,country) before joining) so the multiplication is intentional and correct. | When composing further window functions or computing percentiles across events, treat this view as event-grain canonical input (one row per event) and avoid joins that change row multiplicity without explicit re-aggregation.

earthquakes_rank_by_magnitude_win.description: Assign per-year and per-country ranks to events by a chosen magnitude measure (exposes rank and row_number so callers can filter top-k). Use this when retrieving highest-magnitude events within partitions. | Use for: Select top-N largest magnitude events per country per year; Identify ties in magnitude using rank vs row_number; Compare primary magnitude ranking vs alternative magnitude selection

earthquakes_cumulative_deaths_win_by_yea.name: earthquakes_cumulative_deaths_win_by_year
earthquakes_cumulative_deaths_win_by_yea.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  country,
  SUM(events_in_year) AS events_in_year,
  SUM(deaths_in_year) AS deaths_in_year,
  SUM(SUM(events_in_year)) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_events,
  SUM(SUM(deaths_in_year)) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_deaths
FROM (
  SELECT
    year,
    country,
    COUNT(1) AS events_in_year,
    SUM(IFNULL(deaths,0)) AS deaths_in_year
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes`
  GROUP BY
    year,
    country
)
GROUP BY
  year,
  country
ORDER BY
  country, year

params.description: Yearly per-country counts and cumulative sums of earthquake events and deaths (running totals by year within each country).
params.when_to_use: Show how many earthquake events and deaths occurred in each country each year, plus running totals up through that year for each country. | Trend analysis of earthquake frequency and human impact over time at the country level (year granularity). | Build year-over-year change metrics (e.g., delta events or delta deaths) or visualize cumulative burden by country. | As a pre-aggregated input when composing higher-level aggregations (e.g., multi-country totals by year) or when joining to country metadata/dimensions.
params.output_schema: year: calendar year for the aggregated events (derived from earthquakes.year in the base table) | country: country name or code as reported in the source earthquakes table (derived from earthquakes.country) | events_in_year: number of earthquake events recorded in that country during that year = COUNT(1) grouped by (year, country) from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes` | deaths_in_year: sum of deaths recorded for events in that country and year = SUM(IFNULL(deaths,0)) from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes` | cumulative_events: running total of events for the country up to and including that year = SUM(events_in_year) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) | cumulative_deaths: running total of deaths for the country up to and including that year = SUM(deaths_in_year) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.metric: events_in_year = COUNT(1) grouped by (year, country) over source rows | deaths_in_year = SUM(IFNULL(deaths, 0)) grouped by (year, country) over source rows | cumulative_events = running SUM(events_in_year) partitioned by country ordered by year (i.e., SUM(SUM(events_in_year)) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)) | cumulative_deaths = running SUM(deaths_in_year) partitioned by country ordered by year (i.e., SUM(SUM(deaths_in_year)) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW))
params.composition: Cardinality-safe joins (do not duplicate measures): |  - Join to country-dimension or metadata tables (e.g., country lookup/dim views) on country = country. Safe because this view's grain is one row per (year, country); a one-to-one or many-to-one dimension keyed by country will not multiply rows, so events_in_year and cumulative metrics remain correct. |  - Join to year/calendar dimension on year = year. Safe for the same reason: one row per year per country in this view; joining to a one-to-one year dimension does not duplicate measures. |  | Joins that are NOT safe without re-aggregation or deduplication: |  - Do NOT join directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from (year, country) (for example: raw earthquake events, per-event reports, or other event-level tables keyed to the same year and country) without first aggregating that other table to (year, country) or otherwise ensuring uniqueness. Such joins will multiply rows and over-count events_in_year and deaths_in_year as well as cumulative metrics. |  - Do NOT join to any time-series or path/segment tables (e.g., tornado_paths_enriched_by_date, hurricane_track_points_core) that may contain multiple rows per (year, country) without reducing them to one row per (year, country) first. Multiplying rows will incorrectly inflate counts and running totals. |  | Guidance for correct composition when combining measures: |  - If you need to combine this view with another multi-row-per-(year,country) dataset, first aggregate that dataset to (year, country) with the desired measures, then join the aggregated result to this view on (year, country). After joining two (year, country) level sources you can safely compute combined metrics (sums, rates, ratios). |  - To produce totals across countries for a given year, aggregate this view by year (e.g., SUM(events_in_year) GROUP BY year). Aggregating upward from this view preserves correctness because it is already at a deterministic (year, country) grain. |  - If you need population or area denominators (to compute per-capita rates), join to a country-level denominator table keyed by country (one-row-per-country). That is safe; if the denominator is multi-row per country, pre-aggregate it to one row per country first.

earthquakes_cumulative_deaths_win_by_yea.description: Compute cumulative deaths and event counts over years per country (running totals). Use this for cumulative impact timelines and trend visualization. | Use for: Plot cumulative deaths by country over time; Compute year-to-date totals and compare across countries; Identify years with large incremental increases in impacts

earthquakes_distinct_sets.name: earthquakes_distinct_sets
earthquakes_distinct_sets.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  year,
  country,
  region_code,
  location_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes`
grain: year, country, region_code, location_name -- one row per distinct combination present in source

params.description: A set of distinct year / country / region_code / location_name combinations present in the NOAA significant earthquakes source table.
params.when_to_use: Find all unique locations (location_name) where significant earthquakes were recorded, optionally partitioned by year, country, or region_code. | Drive existence/lookup filters or dimension joins when you need one row per distinct (year, country, region_code, location_name) combination from the earthquakes source. | Compose higher-level aggregates (counts, joins to location or region dims) while avoiding double-counting by using this as a distinct key set.
params.output_schema: year: the event year as present in bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.year | country: the country value as present in bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.country | region_code: the region code as present in bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.region_code | location_name: the textual location_name as present in bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes.location_name
params.metric: This SET view exposes no aggregated numeric metrics. It is a distinct key set: every output column is a direct projection of the base columns (no derived aggregates).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension tables keyed at the same level (one row per location_name or per region_code or per country) without re-aggregation. Example: join to a locations_dim on location_name (JOIN ... ON earthquakes_distinct_sets.location_name = locations_dim.location_name) is safe because earthquakes_distinct_sets contains at most one row per (year,country,region_code,location_name) combination; joining to a one-row-per-location dimension will not multiply measures in queries that treat each row of this view as the unit of analysis. | It is safe to join to a regions or countries dimension on region_code or country respectively, provided those dims are one-row-per-region_code or one-row-per-country. Example safe join: ON earthquakes_distinct_sets.region_code = regions.region_code. | Do NOT naively join this view to any table or view that is one-to-many relative to the (year,country,region_code,location_name) key without re-aggregating the child side first. Examples of unsafe joins that would duplicate rows/measures: joining to raw earthquakes (which is many events per the same combination), event reports (events_point_reports_normalized), or any observations tables (icoads_*, gsod_daily_cleaned) that contain multiple rows per the same location and year. If you must join to a one-to-many table, either: |   - aggregate the many-side to one row per (year,country,region_code,location_name) before joining (e.g., COUNT, SUM, MAX grouped by those keys), or |   - join first and then re-aggregate from the combined result back to the desired grain to avoid multiplication of measures. | When composing time-series or year-level aggregates, note the view includes year as part of its grain. If you need to aggregate across years, group by country/region_code/location_name and remove year, or use a separate aggregation step. | Because this is a DISTINCT set (no numeric measures), it is primarily intended as a dimension/seed for composition rather than a pre-aggregated metric source. Any numeric metrics derived later must be computed with explicit aggregation to maintain correctness.

earthquakes_distinct_sets.description: Provide distinct enumerations useful for cohort building: distinct years, countries, region_codes, and location names. Use this for filters, drop-downs, and set operations. | Use for: Populate UI filters (available years, countries, regions, locations); Compute set differences between cohorts defined by year or country

earthquakes_semantic_labels_region_damag.name: earthquakes_semantic_labels_region_damage
earthquakes_semantic_labels_region_damag.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  region_code,
  CASE
    WHEN region_code = 10 THEN 'Central, Western and S. Africa'
    WHEN region_code = 15 THEN 'Northern Africa'
    WHEN region_code = 20 THEN 'Antarctica'
    WHEN region_code = 30 THEN 'East Asia'
    WHEN region_code = 40 THEN 'Central Asia and Caucasus'
    WHEN region_code = 50 THEN 'Kamchatka and Kuril Islands'
    WHEN region_code = 60 THEN 'S. and SE. Asia and Indian Ocean'
    WHEN region_code = 70 THEN 'Atlantic Ocean'
    WHEN region_code = 80 THEN 'Bering Sea'
    WHEN region_code = 90 THEN 'Caribbean'
    WHEN region_code = 100 THEN 'Central America'
    WHEN region_code = 110 THEN 'Eastern Europe'
    WHEN region_code = 120 THEN 'Northern and Western Europe'
    WHEN region_code = 130 THEN 'Southern Europe'
    WHEN region_code = 140 THEN 'Middle East'
    WHEN region_code = 150 THEN 'North America and Hawaii'
    WHEN region_code = 160 THEN 'South America'
    WHEN region_code = 170 THEN 'Central and South Pacific'
    ELSE 'UNKNOWN_REGION'
  END AS region_label,
  damage_description,
  CASE
    WHEN damage_description = 0 THEN 'NONE'
    WHEN damage_description = 1 THEN 'LIMITED (< $1M approx)'
    WHEN damage_description = 2 THEN 'MODERATE (~$1-$5M)'
    WHEN damage_description = 3 THEN 'SEVERE (~$5-$24M)'
    WHEN damage_description = 4 THEN 'EXTREME (~$25M+)'
    ELSE 'UNKNOWN_DAMAGE_DESC'
  END AS damage_label
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_significant_earthquakes.earthquakes`
grain: id -- one row per event with human-readable region and damage labels

params.description: Provides one human-readable region label and a human-readable damage severity label for each earthquake event id.
params.when_to_use: Look up the region name and damage severity label for a specific earthquake event id. | Join to event-level earthquake datasets when you need readable region and damage labels for reporting, filtering, or grouping at the event (id) grain. | Compose event-level aggregations (counts, sums) grouped by region_label or damage_label after joining this view at the event id level.
params.output_schema: id: the unique event identifier for the earthquake event (derived from base column `id` in the source table). | region_code: numeric region code for the event (directly from base column `region_code`). | region_label: human-readable region name mapped from `region_code` via CASE expressions in the view SQL (e.g. 150 -> 'North America and Hawaii'; unknown codes -> 'UNKNOWN_REGION'). | damage_description: numeric damage description code for the event (directly from base column `damage_description`). | damage_label: human-readable damage severity mapped from `damage_description` via CASE expressions in the view SQL (0 -> 'NONE', 1 -> 'LIMITED (< $1M approx)', 2 -> 'MODERATE (~$1-$5M)', 3 -> 'SEVERE (~$5-$24M)', 4 -> 'EXTREME (~$25M+)', unknown -> 'UNKNOWN_DAMAGE_DESC').
params.metric: No aggregated metrics are defined in this view. All output columns are either direct base columns or deterministic CASE-mapped labels. | region_label = CASE(region_code WHEN 10 THEN 'Central, Western and S. Africa' WHEN 15 THEN 'Northern Africa' WHEN 20 THEN 'Antarctica' WHEN 30 THEN 'East Asia' WHEN 40 THEN 'Central Asia and Caucasus' WHEN 50 THEN 'Kamchatka and Kuril Islands' WHEN 60 THEN 'S. and SE. Asia and Indian Ocean' WHEN 70 THEN 'Atlantic Ocean' WHEN 80 THEN 'Bering Sea' WHEN 90 THEN 'Caribbean' WHEN 100 THEN 'Central America' WHEN 110 THEN 'Eastern Europe' WHEN 120 THEN 'Northern and Western Europe' WHEN 130 THEN 'Southern Europe' WHEN 140 THEN 'Middle East' WHEN 150 THEN 'North America and Hawaii' WHEN 160 THEN 'South America' WHEN 170 THEN 'Central and South Pacific' ELSE 'UNKNOWN_REGION' END | damage_label = CASE(damage_description WHEN 0 THEN 'NONE' WHEN 1 THEN 'LIMITED (< $1M approx)' WHEN 2 THEN 'MODERATE (~$1-$5M)' WHEN 3 THEN 'SEVERE (~$5-$24M)' WHEN 4 THEN 'EXTREME (~$25M+)' ELSE 'UNKNOWN_DAMAGE_DESC' END)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to event-level tables or views on id (e.g., join to earthquakes_core_events_sel ON id) — safe because this view has exactly one row per event id, so joining 1:1 on id will not duplicate rows or measures. | Safe to join to sibling normalized event-level views (NORM/SEL) on id when those siblings are also one-row-per-event (for example: earthquakes_core_events_sel, earthquakes_magnitudes_unpivot if filtered to one magnitude row per event). | Do NOT naively join this view to one-to-many tables or views (for example, any observations, reports, or aggregated-by-date sequences that produce multiple rows per event id) without first aggregating the many-side to one row per event. Joining a one-row-per-event view to a many-row-per-event table will multiply event-level rows and duplicate any derived measures tied to the event row. If you need to combine with a one-to-many relation, either: | - aggregate the many-side to one row per event id (e.g., COUNT(*), SUM(...), MAX(...)) and then join on id, or | - perform the join and then re-aggregate at the desired grain (e.g., GROUP BY this view's region_label and compute aggregates). | Examples of joins that would duplicate rows if done directly: joining to event_point_reports (many reports per event), observation sequences, or any WIN/AGG/RANK sibling views that produce multiple rows per event id without collapsing to one row. | If you need to compute event-counts grouped by region_label or damage_label, prefer: SELECT region_label, COUNT(*) FROM earthquakes_semantic_labels_region_damage GROUP BY region_label; or join first at id then aggregate on the combined result to avoid double-counting.

earthquakes_semantic_labels_region_damag.description: Expose region and damage description labels derived from coded columns (maps region_code and damage_description to human-readable labels). Use when presenting readable categories in reports. | Use for: Display readable region and damage categories in dashboards and reports; Group by region_label or damage_label for aggregates

historical_runups_core_sel.name: historical_runups_core_sel
historical_runups_core_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  tsevent_id,
  TIMESTAMP(timestamp) AS event_timestamp_utc,
  year,
  month,
  day,
  arr_day,
  arr_hour,
  arr_min,
  doubtful,
  country,
  state AS state_prov_prefecture,
  location_name,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  region_code,
  distance_from_source,
  travel_time_hours,
  travel_time_minutes,
  type_measurement_id,
  water_ht,
  horizontal_inundation,
  period,
  first_motion,
  deaths,
  injuries,
  damage_millions_dollars,
  houses_damaged,
  houses_destroyed
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups`
grain: id -- one row per reported runup observation

params.description: Provides one-row-per-reported historical tsunami runup observation with location, timing, measurement and impact attributes (water height, inundation, casualties, damage, houses affected).
params.when_to_use: List or filter historical runup observations by time, location, measurement type, or impact (e.g., find all runups in a country/year or above a water height). | Join as the canonical set of individual runup observations when composing event-level summaries (after appropriate aggregation) or when enriching runups with external dimensions keyed by event/runup id. | Build aggregates (counts, sums, averages) of runup metrics (water_ht, horizontal_inundation, deaths, injuries, damage_millions_dollars, houses_damaged, houses_destroyed) by grouping on year, country, region_code, tsevent_id, etc. | Filter and map runup spatial distributions (latitude/longitude) and travel/time characteristics (distance_from_source, travel_time_hours/minutes) for visualization or spatial analysis.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the runup observation (derived from historical_runups.id) | tsevent_id: identifier of the parent tsunami event associated with this runup (derived from historical_runups.tsevent_id) | event_timestamp_utc: timestamp of the reported observation cast to TIMESTAMP (derived from historical_runups.timestamp) | year: integer year of the observation (derived from historical_runups.year) | month: integer month of the observation (derived from historical_runups.month) | day: integer day of the observation (derived from historical_runups.day) | arr_day: arrival day marker as provided in source (derived from historical_runups.arr_day) | arr_hour: arrival hour marker as provided in source (derived from historical_runups.arr_hour) | arr_min: arrival minute marker as provided in source (derived from historical_runups.arr_min) | doubtful: flag indicating doubtful observations (derived from historical_runups.doubtful) | country: country name where the runup was observed (derived from historical_runups.country) | state_prov_prefecture: state / province / prefecture (renamed from historical_runups.state) | location_name: textual location description (derived from historical_runups.location_name) | latitude: observation latitude in decimal degrees (derived from historical_runups.latitude) | longitude: observation longitude in decimal degrees (derived from historical_runups.longitude) | region_code: region code assigned in source (derived from historical_runups.region_code) | distance_from_source: reported distance from tsunami source (derived from historical_runups.distance_from_source) | travel_time_hours: travel time in hours as reported (derived from historical_runups.travel_time_hours) | travel_time_minutes: travel time minutes component as reported (derived from historical_runups.travel_time_minutes) | type_measurement_id: numeric id of measurement type (derived from historical_runups.type_measurement_id) | water_ht: reported water height (derived from historical_runups.water_ht) | horizontal_inundation: reported horizontal inundation distance/extent (derived from historical_runups.horizontal_inundation) | period: reported wave period (derived from historical_runups.period) | first_motion: reported first motion description (derived from historical_runups.first_motion) | deaths: reported deaths attributable to this runup observation (derived from historical_runups.deaths) | injuries: reported injuries (derived from historical_runups.injuries) | damage_millions_dollars: reported damage in millions of dollars (derived from historical_runups.damage_millions_dollars) | houses_damaged: number of houses damaged (derived from historical_runups.houses_damaged) | houses_destroyed: number of houses destroyed (derived from historical_runups.houses_destroyed)
params.metric: water_ht = direct source column (no aggregation) — use aggregate functions (AVG, MAX, SUM) when computing over groups | horizontal_inundation = direct source column (no aggregation) — aggregate as needed | deaths = direct source column (no aggregation) — represents deaths reported for that runup row; to get event-level or regional totals, SUM(deaths) grouped by tsevent_id or region_code | injuries = direct source column (no aggregation) — aggregate with SUM when composing higher-level metrics | damage_millions_dollars = direct source column (no aggregation) — aggregate with SUM to get total damage | houses_damaged = direct source column (no aggregation) — aggregate with SUM for totals | houses_destroyed = direct source column (no aggregation) — aggregate with SUM for totals | travel_time_total_minutes = travel_time_hours * 60 + travel_time_minutes (not present in view; computed expression should be derived by planners when needed)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to tsunami_events_core_sel on tsevent_id = tsunami_events_core_sel.id — safe because this view is one row per runup (id) and tsunami_events_core_sel is one row per event id; joining adds event-level attributes without duplicating runup measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to any date dimension keyed by (year, month, day) or event_timestamp_utc (e.g., a calendar table) — safe because those joins are many-to-one from this runup view to the date dim, so measures on this view remain per-runup. | cardinality-SAFE: join to geographic/dimension tables keyed by country or region_code where the dimension is one-row-per-country/region — safe because runup rows remain unique and measures are not duplicated. | DO NOT join without aggregation to one-to-many sources keyed to runup id (bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.id) such as a hypothetical observations log or multiple-measurements-per-runup table — such a join would duplicate runup-level measures (deaths, water_ht, etc.). Instead, pre-aggregate the many-side to one row per runup id (e.g., SUM or MAX) before joining back. | DO NOT join this view directly to sibling AGG or RANK views that are computed at different grains (e.g., historical_runups_year_country_agg) expecting to preserve this view's row-level measures — if you need aggregated metrics from those views, either (a) aggregate this view to the same grain and then join on matching keys, or (b) join event/runup keys to bring event-level aggregates into each runup row understanding that aggregated measures will repeat per runup. | When composing event-level summaries: aggregate this view first (GROUP BY tsevent_id) to compute SUM(deaths) or AVG(water_ht) per event, and then join to event-level tables. This prevents double-counting if you later join to other runup-related tables.

historical_runups_core_sel.description: Selectable projection of core runup attributes for mapping, filtering or lightweight joins. Use this to quickly restrict to descriptive columns (id, tsevent_id, timestamp, date parts, location, lat/lon, country/state, region_code) plus key measures (water_ht, horizontal_inundation, deaths, injuries, damage_millions_dollars). Good as a starting point for WHERE-filtered cohorts (by country, region, year, doubtful flag, measurement type). | Use for: List or map runup observations for a country/region/time period; Filter to non-doubtful observations or specific measurement types; Join with an external events table on tsevent_id

historical_runups_year_country_agg.name: historical_runups_year_country_agg
historical_runups_year_country_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  country,
  region_code,
  COUNT(1) AS observations_count,
  COUNTIF(doubtful IS NULL OR doubtful = '') AS non_doubtful_count,
  COUNTIF(doubtful IS NOT NULL AND doubtful <> '') AS doubtful_count,
  MIN(water_ht) AS min_water_ht_m,
  AVG(water_ht) AS avg_water_ht_m,
  MAX(water_ht) AS max_water_ht_m,
  MIN(horizontal_inundation) AS min_horizontal_inundation_m,
  AVG(horizontal_inundation) AS avg_horizontal_inundation_m,
  MAX(horizontal_inundation) AS max_horizontal_inundation_m,
  SUM(IFNULL(deaths,0)) AS sum_deaths,
  SUM(IFNULL(injuries,0)) AS sum_injuries,
  SUM(IFNULL(damage_millions_dollars,0)) AS sum_damage_millions_dollars,
  SUM(IFNULL(houses_damaged,0)) AS sum_houses_damaged,
  SUM(IFNULL(houses_destroyed,0)) AS sum_houses_destroyed
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups`
GROUP BY year, country, region_code

params.description: Year / country / region_code-level aggregates of historical tsunami runup observations: counts, water height and inundation statistics, and summed impact metrics (deaths, injuries, damage, houses).
params.when_to_use: Get annual summaries of tsunami runup observations per country and region_code (e.g., how many observations, totals of deaths/injuries/damage). | Compare water height or inundation statistics (min/avg/max) by year and country or produce time series of aggregated impact metrics. | As a building block for dashboards or reports that need pre-aggregated yearly country-level tsunami impact and measure summaries. | Join with country or region dimension tables (one-row-per-country or per-region) to enrich with names or regions without changing measures. | As input to further aggregation (e.g., aggregate to multi-year, regional or global totals) or to compute rates per population after joining to population dimension (join must be one-to-one on country/year).
params.output_schema: year: calendar year of the runup observation (source: historical_runups.year) | country: country identifier string from the source table (source: historical_runups.country) | region_code: region code string from the source table (source: historical_runups.region_code) | observations_count: COUNT(1) of raw rows in historical_runups for that (year, country, region_code) group — total number of observations | non_doubtful_count: COUNTIF(doubtful IS NULL OR doubtful = '') — number of observations not marked as doubtful (derived from historical_runups.doubtful) | doubtful_count: COUNTIF(doubtful IS NOT NULL AND doubtful <> '') — number of observations marked as doubtful (derived from historical_runups.doubtful) | min_water_ht_m: MIN(water_ht) — minimum water height (meters) in the group (source: historical_runups.water_ht) | avg_water_ht_m: AVG(water_ht) — average water height (meters) in the group (source: historical_runups.water_ht) | max_water_ht_m: MAX(water_ht) — maximum water height (meters) in the group (source: historical_runups.water_ht) | min_horizontal_inundation_m: MIN(horizontal_inundation) — minimum horizontal inundation (meters) in the group (source: historical_runups.horizontal_inundation) | avg_horizontal_inundation_m: AVG(horizontal_inundation) — average horizontal inundation (meters) in the group (source: historical_runups.horizontal_inundation) | max_horizontal_inundation_m: MAX(horizontal_inundation) — maximum horizontal inundation (meters) in the group (source: historical_runups.horizontal_inundation) | sum_deaths: SUM(IFNULL(deaths,0)) — sum of deaths (treating NULL as 0) in the group (source: historical_runups.deaths) | sum_injuries: SUM(IFNULL(injuries,0)) — sum of injuries (treating NULL as 0) in the group (source: historical_runups.injuries) | sum_damage_millions_dollars: SUM(IFNULL(damage_millions_dollars,0)) — sum of reported damage in millions USD (NULL treated as 0) in the group (source: historical_runups.damage_millions_dollars) | sum_houses_damaged: SUM(IFNULL(houses_damaged,0)) — sum of houses damaged (NULL treated as 0) in the group (source: historical_runups.houses_damaged) | sum_houses_destroyed: SUM(IFNULL(houses_destroyed,0)) — sum of houses destroyed (NULL treated as 0) in the group (source: historical_runups.houses_destroyed)
params.metric: observations_count = COUNT(1) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | non_doubtful_count = COUNTIF(doubtful IS NULL OR doubtful = '') over grouping (year, country, region_code) | doubtful_count = COUNTIF(doubtful IS NOT NULL AND doubtful <> '') over grouping (year, country, region_code) | min_water_ht_m = MIN(water_ht) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | avg_water_ht_m = AVG(water_ht) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | max_water_ht_m = MAX(water_ht) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | min_horizontal_inundation_m = MIN(horizontal_inundation) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | avg_horizontal_inundation_m = AVG(horizontal_inundation) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | max_horizontal_inundation_m = MAX(horizontal_inundation) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | sum_deaths = SUM(COALESCE(deaths,0)) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | sum_injuries = SUM(COALESCE(injuries,0)) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | sum_damage_millions_dollars = SUM(COALESCE(damage_millions_dollars,0)) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | sum_houses_damaged = SUM(COALESCE(houses_damaged,0)) over grouping (year, country, region_code) | sum_houses_destroyed = SUM(COALESCE(houses_destroyed,0)) over grouping (year, country, region_code)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to a country dimension (one-row-per-country) on country — safe because this view is at (year,country,region_code) grain and a country dim is one-row-per-country; measures will not be duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE: join to a region dimension (one-row-per-region_code) on region_code — safe for the same reason as above. | cardinality-SAFE: aggregate this view up first before joining to multi-year or multi-geography aggregates. Example: to get country-level totals across years, SELECT country, SUM(sum_deaths) FROM historical_runups_year_country_agg GROUP BY country — safe because sums are additive. | NOT safe without re-aggregation: do NOT join directly to any table/view that is one-to-many from (year,country,region_code) such as raw historical_runups rows or any event-level tables (e.g., historical_runups_core_sel) without re-aggregating the other side to the same (year,country,region_code) grain — doing so will multiply the aggregated measures and produce incorrect totals. | NOT safe without re-aggregation: do NOT join to views that contain multiple rows per country-year (for example, event-level reports, stations, or path geometries) unless you first aggregate those views to exactly the (year, country, region_code) keys or otherwise join on a key that enforces one-to-one. | safe composition pattern: to enrich aggregated metrics with attributes from another table that is many-to-one to this view (e.g., country population per year), ensure the enrichment table is exactly one-row-per-(year,country) or pre-aggregate it to that grain. Then join on (year,country) and treat region_code carefully (use NULL or join on region_code if available). | safe composition pattern for further aggregation: this view's additive metrics (sum_deaths, sum_injuries, sum_damage_millions_dollars, sum_houses_damaged, sum_houses_destroyed, observations_count) can be summed across groups (e.g., to region or global) without losing correctness. Non-additive stats (min/avg/max) should be recomputed if you require correct global or higher-level min/avg/max from raw data, or approximate by combining mins and maxes (min of mins, max of maxes). For avg_water_ht_m and avg_horizontal_inundation_m: to compute a true aggregated average across groups you must weight by the contributing observation counts or recompute from raw rows; e.g., global_avg = SUM(avg_water_ht_m * observations_count) / SUM(observations_count).

historical_runups_year_country_agg.description: Yearly aggregated measures by country and region_code. Produces counts and common summaries (min/avg/max) for numeric measures such as water_ht, horizontal_inundation, deaths, injuries, damage and houses damaged/destroyed. Use this for trend analysis, country-year summaries, or as input to ranking and time-series windows. | Use for: Yearly totals and averages of runup impact by country or region; Trend analysis of average or maximum water height per country/year; Country-year comparisons of deaths, injuries, or monetary damage

historical_runups_top_waterht_rank.name: historical_runups_top_waterht_rank
historical_runups_top_waterht_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  tsevent_id,
  year,
  country,
  region_code,
  location_name,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  water_ht,
  type_measurement_id,
  doubtful,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country, year ORDER BY water_ht DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_water_ht_desc,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country, year ORDER BY water_ht DESC NULLS LAST, id) AS rownum_by_water_ht_desc
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups`
grain: id -- one row per original runup observation augmented with per-(country,year) rank

params.description: Provides per-original-runup observation rows augmented with within-(country,year) rank and row-number ordered by measured water height (descending), enabling selection of top runups per country-year or composition into further aggregations.
params.when_to_use: Find the top N historical runup observations by water height for each country and year | Select the single highest runup (rank = 1) per country-year | Filter or inspect runup observations together with their relative rank within the same country and year | Compose with other dimensions (e.g., event or country attributes) when you need the original observation-level granularity plus its within-group rank | Build derived aggregations (counts, max water_ht per rank) while preserving correct ranking-aware semantics
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier of the original runup observation — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.id | tsevent_id: foreign key referencing the tsunami event associated with the runup observation — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.tsevent_id | year: observation year (used as the partitioning year for ranking) — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.year | country: country name/code for the observation (partitioning key for ranking) — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.country | region_code: regional code where the observation occurred — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.region_code | location_name: human-readable location name for the observation — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.location_name | latitude: observation latitude (decimal degrees) — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.latitude | longitude: observation longitude (decimal degrees) — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.longitude | water_ht: measured runup water height (numeric) used for ranking — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.water_ht | type_measurement_id: measurement type identifier describing how water_ht was measured — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.type_measurement_id | doubtful: boolean/flag indicating doubtful observation status — from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.doubtful | rank_by_water_ht_desc: RANK() over (PARTITION BY country, year ORDER BY water_ht DESC NULLS LAST) — 1 = highest water_ht within that country-year; ties receive same rank | rownum_by_water_ht_desc: ROW_NUMBER() over (PARTITION BY country, year ORDER BY water_ht DESC NULLS LAST, id) — stable unique row sequence within country-year (no ties), useful for deterministic top-N selection
params.metric: rank_by_water_ht_desc = RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY country, year ORDER BY water_ht DESC NULLS LAST) -- analytic rank, ties allowed; smaller = higher measured runup | rownum_by_water_ht_desc = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country, year ORDER BY water_ht DESC NULLS LAST, id) -- deterministic unique position per row within country-year
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a country-dimension or region lookup on country or region_code (e.g., countries_dim.country = historical_runups_top_waterht_rank.country) — safe because this view is one-row-per-original-observation; joining to a 1-to-1 or many-to-1 dimension will not duplicate rows or measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to tsunami_events_core_sel (or other event-level view) on tsevent_id = tsunami_events_core_sel.id — safe (many runup observations may map to the same event, but this view is at runup-observation grain and contains no aggregated measures; joining to event-level 1-to-1 info will not duplicate the runup rows). | do NOT blindly join to one-to-many child tables (for the runup's id) without re-aggregation first, e.g., joining to a table of multiple photos/notes per runup_id will multiply rows and therefore duplicate rank/measure semantics. If you need aggregates over those children, pre-aggregate the child table to one row per runup.id (SUM/COUNT/MAX as appropriate) before joining. | do NOT join to another ranking view partitioned differently (e.g., a view that ranks by region rather than country) expecting preserved counts: if you join two ranked result sets one-to-many you'll alter cardinality; instead join on keys and then re-compute desired ranking/aggregation in a single query or aggregate after the join. | When composing higher-level aggregates (for example, 'max water_ht per country-year' using this view), prefer re-aggregating water_ht from this view (MAX(water_ht) GROUP BY country, year) rather than summing or counting rank fields. Because rank_by_water_ht_desc is an analytic attribute, it is not an additive metric — treat it as descriptive metadata, not as a measure to aggregate. | If you need a top-N per country-year and then to attach additional many-side details, first filter this view to the desired top-N using rownum_by_water_ht_desc (e.g., WHERE rownum_by_water_ht_desc <= N) to produce a bounded set, then join to other tables; this prevents accidental large joins and preserves intended top-N semantics.

historical_runups_top_waterht_rank.description: Assigns per-country and per-year ranks by water_ht to identify the highest runups. Exposes rank_by_water_ht_desc so downstream queries can select top-N by filtering on rank <= K. Keeps original identifying columns for joins. | Use for: Select top-N highest runups per country-year or per country across years; Find locations with the single highest recorded water_ht per country/year

historical_runups_time_series_win.name: historical_runups_time_series_win
historical_runups_time_series_win.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  tsevent_id,
  TIMESTAMP(timestamp) AS event_timestamp_utc,
  year,
  country,
  region_code,
  deaths,
  water_ht,
  SUM(IFNULL(deaths,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY TIMESTAMP(timestamp) ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_deaths_by_country,
  AVG(water_ht) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY TIMESTAMP(timestamp) ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS rolling_avg_water_ht_10_events
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups`
grain: id -- one row per runup observation with windowed cumulative and rolling aggregates per country

params.description: Time-series of historical tsunami runup observations with per-country cumulative deaths and a 10-event rolling average of water height, at the per-observation grain.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve runup-level events (one row per runup observation) with country-level running cumulative deaths up to each observation. | Compute recent/local trends in water height per country using a 10-event trailing average (rolling window) aligned to each observation. | Compose time-ordered country-level cumulative or rolling metrics into downstream analyses while preserving the original observation detail. | Join to event- or observation-level detail (e.g., report text or coordinates) without duplicating cumulative or rolling measures if join keys are one-to-one.
params.output_schema: id: unique identifier for the runup observation (derived from historical_runups.id). | tsevent_id: id of the related tsunami event (derived from historical_runups.tsevent_id). | event_timestamp_utc: event timestamp converted to TIMESTAMP type (derived from historical_runups.timestamp). | year: year of the observation (derived from historical_runups.year). | country: country name for the observation (derived from historical_runups.country). | region_code: region code associated with the observation (derived from historical_runups.region_code). | deaths: death count recorded for this runup observation (derived from historical_runups.deaths). | water_ht: measured runup water height for this observation (derived from historical_runups.water_ht). | cumulative_deaths_by_country: running sum of deaths for the country ordered by timestamp up to and including this row (defined using SUM(IFNULL(deaths,0)) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY TIMESTAMP(timestamp) ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) on historical_runups.deaths). | rolling_avg_water_ht_10_events: trailing moving average of water_ht across the current and previous 9 observations within the same country ordered by timestamp (defined using AVG(water_ht) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY TIMESTAMP(timestamp) ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) on historical_runups.water_ht).
params.metric: cumulative_deaths_by_country = SUM(IFNULL(deaths, 0)) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY TIMESTAMP(timestamp) ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) | rolling_avg_water_ht_10_events = AVG(water_ht) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY TIMESTAMP(timestamp) ROWS BETWEEN 9 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to event-level or event-dimension views (e.g., tsunami_events_core_sel) on tsevent_id — safe because this view is at one row per runup observation (id) and joining on tsevent_id to a one-row-per-event table will not duplicate the view's measures provided the event-side is one-row-per-tsevent_id. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a station/location dimension that is one-row-per-region_code or one-row-per-country on region_code or country — safe because region_code/country on the dimension are keys with single rows per key, so cumulative and rolling measures remain aligned to each observation row. | unsafe join warning: do NOT join directly to any table or view that is one-to-many relative to a runup observation (for example, a table containing multiple reports, sensor readings, or measurements per runup id) without first aggregating the many-side to the runup-observation key (id) because that will multiply rows and therefore duplicate cumulative_deaths_by_country and rolling_avg_water_ht_10_events. | unsafe join warning: do NOT join to sibling WIN or AGG views that produce multiple rows per the same runup observation id (or per country/timestamp partitions overlapping these rows) unless you re-aggregate or deduplicate first — window functions here assume ordering per country and will be incorrectly expanded if duplicates are introduced. | recommended composition pattern: when combining with one-to-many data (e.g., per-observation sensor series), first aggregate the many-side to one row per id (or per tsevent_id if joining on that key) using SUM/AVG/COUNT as appropriate, then join to this view to preserve meaning of cumulative and rolling metrics. | ordering/temporal composition note: window calculations are computed using TIMESTAMP(timestamp) ordering. If downstream composition changes ordering (e.g., joining to a different timestamp field), recompute rolling/cumulative metrics in that context rather than assuming they remain valid.

historical_runups_time_series_win.description: Windowed time-series measures per country: event-level running cumulative sums and moving averages of deaths and water_ht when ordered by timestamp. Useful for cumulative impact plots or rolling summaries. Exposes cumulative_deaths and rolling_avg_water_ht (window size expressed as number of events via RANGE or ROWS can be adjusted downstream). | Use for: Cumulative deaths over time for a country; Rolling average water height per country to smooth extremes

historical_runups_measure_type_counts_re.name: historical_runups_measure_type_counts_reshape
historical_runups_measure_type_counts_re.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  country,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_1_eyewitness,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_2_tide_gauge,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_3_deep_ocean_gauge,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_4_post_survey_water_ht,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_5_runup_height_post_survey,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_6_atmospheric_wave,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_7_seiche,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_8_runup_in_harbor,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 9 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_9_splash_mark,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt_type_10_flow_depth,
  COUNT(1) AS total_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups`
GROUP BY year, country

params.description: Counts of historical tsunami runup measurements by measurement type, aggregated to year × country (one row per year and country).
params.when_to_use: Get how many runup measurements of each measurement type occurred in a given year and country. | Build time-series or country comparisons of measurement-type distributions (e.g., percent eyewitness vs gauge) by year. | As a pre-aggregated base when computing higher-level aggregates (e.g., regional totals across countries or multi-year totals) without scanning raw measurements. | Filterable breakdown when joining to year- or country-level dimension tables to add labels or hierarchies (provided joins remain one-to-one).
params.output_schema: year: calendar year for the measurement(s). Source: historical_runups.year | country: country name / code field from source. Source: historical_runups.country | cnt_type_1_eyewitness: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 1 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) over grouped rows in historical_runups. | cnt_type_2_tide_gauge: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 2 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). | cnt_type_3_deep_ocean_gauge: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 3 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). | cnt_type_4_post_survey_water_ht: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 4 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). | cnt_type_5_runup_height_post_survey: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 5 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). | cnt_type_6_atmospheric_wave: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 6 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). | cnt_type_7_seiche: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 7 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). | cnt_type_8_runup_in_harbor: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 8 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). | cnt_type_9_splash_mark: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 9 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 9 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). | cnt_type_10_flow_depth: integer count of rows where type_measurement_id = 10 within group. Derived from SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). | total_count: integer total number of runup measurement rows in the year × country group. Derived from COUNT(1) over grouped rows in historical_runups.
params.metric: cnt_type_1_eyewitness = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 1 within (year,country) | cnt_type_2_tide_gauge = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 2 within (year,country) | cnt_type_3_deep_ocean_gauge = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 3 within (year,country) | cnt_type_4_post_survey_water_ht = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 4 within (year,country) | cnt_type_5_runup_height_post_survey = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 5 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 5 within (year,country) | cnt_type_6_atmospheric_wave = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 6 within (year,country) | cnt_type_7_seiche = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 7 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 7 within (year,country) | cnt_type_8_runup_in_harbor = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 8 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 8 within (year,country) | cnt_type_9_splash_mark = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 9 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 9 within (year,country) | cnt_type_10_flow_depth = SUM(CASE WHEN type_measurement_id = 10 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)  -- count of rows with type_measurement_id = 10 within (year,country) | total_count = COUNT(1)  -- total rows in historical_runups for the (year,country) group
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a year-level dimension (e.g., a calendar table keyed by year) on year — safe because the calendar table is one-row-per-year and will not duplicate this view's rows, so the counts remain correct. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a country dimension (one-row-per-country) on country — safe because the country dimension is one-row-per-country and will not multiply the aggregated measures. | do NOT join this view directly to historical_runups (the underlying detail table) or to any other table/view that is one-to-many from (year,country) to avoid duplicating its pre-aggregated counts. If you must combine with detail-level tables, either: | - re-aggregate after the join (e.g., SUM(cnt_type_1_eyewitness) GROUP BY ...) to remove duplication, or | - join on a stricter key that ensures one-to-one (for example join on year,country and a unique id) — only valid if the other side is one-row-per-(year,country). | do NOT join to sibling AGG/RESHAPE views that are themselves aggregated at a finer grain (e.g., per-event or per-measure rows) without re-aggregation; those joins can multiply counts unless the sibling view is explicitly one-row-per-(year,country). | Examples of safe compositions: aggregating these counts up to a region by joining to a country→region mapping (one-row-per-country) and then summing the count columns grouped by region — this preserves correctness because the mapping is one-to-one from country to its single region row. | If combining with other pre-aggregated views at the same grain (year,country) you can join on (year,country) and then SUM or compute ratios across the aligned columns. Ensure both inputs are truly one-row-per-(year,country) to avoid duplication.

historical_runups_measure_type_counts_re.description: Counts of observations by type_measurement_id per country and year (unpivot/pivot style). Useful for understanding measurement-method distribution (tide gauge vs eyewitness vs survey). Produces one row per country-year with counts per measurement type as columns. | Use for: Distribution of measurement types across countries or years; Filter countries by predominant measurement method

historical_runups_distinct_sets.name: historical_runups_distinct_sets
historical_runups_distinct_sets.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  year,
  country,
  region_code,
  location_name
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups`
grain: year, country, region_code, location_name -- one row per distinct combination

params.description: Distinct set of year × country × region_code × location_name combinations observed in the NOAA historical_runups table — use to know which unique locations had runup records in which years and countries.
params.when_to_use: List all distinct (year, country, region_code, location_name) combinations present in historical runup data. | Filter or enumerate years, countries, regions, or locations that have any runup records. | Seed downstream analyses that need the distinct location-year membership (e.g., join with location dimension tables, or to left-join aggregated measures per distinct set). | Validate presence/coverage of runup observations across time and geography before aggregating measures.
params.output_schema: year: calendar year value for the runup record — derived from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.year` | country: country name or code as recorded for the runup — derived from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.country` | region_code: region identifier (as recorded in the source) for the runup location — derived from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.region_code` | location_name: textual location name for the runup observation — derived from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_runups.location_name`
params.metric: This view contains no numeric aggregates/metrics. All output columns are distinct key columns projected from the base table: year = year (identity), country = country (identity), region_code = region_code (identity), location_name = location_name (identity).
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a dimension table (e.g., a location or region dimension) on matching keys is safe when the dimension is 1:1 on the join keys. Example: join to a locations_dim on (region_code, location_name) — safe because this view has at most one row per (year,country,region_code,location_name) combination; joining to a 1:1 dimension will not duplicate these rows' meaning or counts. | You may safely left-join aggregated metrics that are defined per (year, country, region_code, location_name) (i.e., pre-aggregated to the same grain) without changing cardinality. Ensure the aggregator produces at most one row per key before joining. | Do NOT join this view directly to a one-to-many detail table (for example, the raw historical_runups table or any other table with multiple records per the same location and year) without re-aggregation, because such joins will duplicate the distinct-set rows and multiply any measures derived after the join. If you need measures from a child/detail table, first aggregate that table to the same grain (year, country, region_code, location_name), then join. | Do NOT join to sibling views that are at a finer grain (e.g., per-observation or per-event views like historical_runups_core_sel or time-series windows) without aggregating them to the distinct-sets grain; otherwise the planner will create many-to-one expansions that multiply the distinct-set rows. | If composing higher-level aggregations across years or countries (e.g., counts of distinct locations per year), use this view as the deduplicated input and then apply COUNT(*) or COUNT(location_name) grouped by the desired keys — this avoids double-counting that would occur if starting from the raw runups table.

historical_runups_distinct_sets.description: Distinct sets for fast lookup: distinct years, countries, region_codes and location_names present in the runups table. Useful for building filters, UI lists or validating allowed values. | Use for: Populate filter dropdowns (years, countries, locations); Verify which region_codes appear for a given country/year
