GROUP BY year, country, region_code

params.description: Year + country + region_code level aggregates of tsunami event counts and summed impact measures (deaths, missing, injuries, damage, houses destroyed/damaged, and total variants).
params.when_to_use: Get annual tsunami event counts and summed impacts by country and region (e.g., 'How many tsunami events and total deaths occurred in Japan in 2011?'). | Feed as a pre-aggregated source when composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., regional, multi-year, or global totals) without having to re-scan raw events. | Join to country or region dimension tables to add names/attributes without changing numeric totals (one-row-per year-country-region). | Build time series, ranking, or trend analyses at year × country × region_code grain.
params.output_schema: year: event year (derived from the base column `year` in bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event) | country: country name or code as stored in `country` in bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event | region_code: region identifier as stored in `region_code` in bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event | events_count: count of source rows (COUNT(1)) per year/country/region_code — number of tsunami events in the group | sum_deaths: SUM(COALESCE(deaths,0)) — sum of the `deaths` column for events in the group | sum_missing: SUM(COALESCE(missing,0)) — sum of the `missing` column for events in the group | sum_injuries: SUM(COALESCE(injuries,0)) — sum of the `injuries` column for events in the group | sum_damage_millions_dollars: SUM(COALESCE(damage_millions_dollars,0)) — sum of `damage_millions_dollars` for events in the group | sum_houses_destroyed: SUM(COALESCE(houses_destroyed,0)) — sum of `houses_destroyed` for events in the group | sum_houses_damaged: SUM(COALESCE(houses_damaged,0)) — sum of `houses_damaged` for events in the group | sum_total_deaths: SUM(COALESCE(total_deaths,0)) — sum of `total_deaths` for events in the group | sum_total_missing: SUM(COALESCE(total_missing,0)) — sum of `total_missing` for events in the group | sum_total_injuries: SUM(COALESCE(total_injuries,0)) — sum of `total_injuries` for events in the group | sum_total_damage_millions_dollars: SUM(COALESCE(total_damage_in_millions_dollars,0)) — sum of `total_damage_in_millions_dollars` for events in the group
params.metric: events_count = COUNT(1) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_deaths = SUM(COALESCE(deaths, 0)) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_missing = SUM(COALESCE(missing, 0)) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_injuries = SUM(COALESCE(injuries, 0)) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_damage_millions_dollars = SUM(COALESCE(damage_millions_dollars, 0)) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_houses_destroyed = SUM(COALESCE(houses_destroyed, 0)) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_houses_damaged = SUM(COALESCE(houses_damaged, 0)) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_total_deaths = SUM(COALESCE(total_deaths, 0)) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_total_missing = SUM(COALESCE(total_missing, 0)) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_total_injuries = SUM(COALESCE(total_injuries, 0)) per (year, country, region_code) | sum_total_damage_millions_dollars = SUM(COALESCE(total_damage_in_millions_dollars, 0)) per (year, country, region_code)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE: join to a country dimension (e.g., countries_dim) on country — safe because this view is one row per (year, country, region_code) so enriching with one-row-per-country attributes does not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE: join to a region/region_code dimension on region_code — safe when the region dimension has at most one row per region_code. | cardinality-SAFE: aggregate this view further (e.g., SUM(events_count) GROUP BY year or country) to produce higher-level totals without re-scanning raw events. | NOT safe to join directly to any one-to-many table keyed to (year, country, region_code) that contains multiple rows per those keys (for example: raw event detail, event reports, or any detailed observation table) without re-aggregation — doing so will multiply the aggregated measures. If you must join to a one-to-many child, first aggregate the child to the same grain (year, country, region_code) before joining or join on strictly one-to-one keys. | If joining to other pre-aggregated views, ensure their grain is equal to or coarser than (year, country, region_code). If their grain is coarser, aggregate this view up to that coarser grain before joining to avoid duplication. | When composing time-series (e.g., summing across years), use SUM(...) over the aggregates (e.g., SUM(events_count)) rather than re-joining back to the base events table.

tsunami_events_year_country_agg.description: Yearly aggregation of event counts and summed impacts by country and region. Useful for trend analysis and comparing annual impact across countries or regions. | Use for: Annual totals of events and impacts by country or region; Time-series charts of deaths/damage by country; Comparing per-year event frequency across regions

tsunami_topmeasures_rank.name: tsunami_topmeasures_rank
tsunami_topmeasures_rank.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  year,
  country,
  location_name,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  primary_magnitude,
  maximum_water_height,
  deaths,
  total_damage_in_millions_dollars,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY year ORDER BY primary_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_magnitude_desc_by_year,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY year ORDER BY maximum_water_height DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_maxwaterht_desc_by_year,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY year ORDER BY deaths DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_deaths_desc_by_year,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER(PARTITION BY year ORDER BY total_damage_in_millions_dollars DESC NULLS LAST) AS rank_by_damage_desc_by_year,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER(ORDER BY primary_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST, maximum_water_height DESC NULLS LAST) AS global_rownum_by_mag_water
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event`
grain: id -- one row per event with rank columns

params.description: Per-event ranks and global row numbers for historical tsunami events, providing year-partitioned ranks by magnitude, maximum water height, deaths, and damage, plus a global ordering by magnitude then water height.
params.when_to_use: Find the top N tsunami events in a given year by magnitude, water height, deaths, or damage (e.g., 'top 5 tsunamis in 1960 by magnitude'). | Filter events by a rank threshold within the same year (e.g., 'events in 1983 with rank_by_deaths_desc_by_year <= 3'). | Combine event-level attributes with other event-level dimensions (country, location, coordinates) when you need pre-computed year-based ranks. | Compose additional aggregations or time-series on a set of ranked events (for example, count of top-3 events per country per decade) — but re-aggregate after joins to avoid double-counting. | Create leaderboards or report cards that need stable per-year ranks and a reproducible global sort by magnitude+water height.
params.output_schema: id: unique event id from base table `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.id` (one row per event, this is the grain). | year: event year from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.year` (used as the partition key for year-based ranks). | country: event country from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.country` (dimension for grouping/filters). | location_name: event location_name from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.location_name` (human-readable place). | latitude: event latitude from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.latitude` (point geometry coordinate). | longitude: event longitude from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.longitude` (point geometry coordinate). | primary_magnitude: event primary_magnitude from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.primary_magnitude` (numeric magnitude used to rank events). | maximum_water_height: event maximum_water_height from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.maximum_water_height` (numeric water height used to rank events). | deaths: event deaths from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.deaths` (numeric casualties used to rank events). | total_damage_in_millions_dollars: event total_damage_in_millions_dollars from `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.total_damage_in_millions_dollars` (numeric economic damage used to rank events). | rank_by_magnitude_desc_by_year: integer dense rank computed as DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY primary_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST) — 1 = largest magnitude in that year; ties share the same rank. | rank_by_maxwaterht_desc_by_year: integer dense rank computed as DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY maximum_water_height DESC NULLS LAST) — 1 = largest maximum water height in that year; ties share the same rank. | rank_by_deaths_desc_by_year: integer dense rank computed as DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY deaths DESC NULLS LAST) — 1 = most deaths in that year; ties share the same rank. | rank_by_damage_desc_by_year: integer dense rank computed as DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY total_damage_in_millions_dollars DESC NULLS LAST) — 1 = largest damage in that year; ties share the same rank. | global_rownum_by_mag_water: integer row number computed as ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY primary_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST, maximum_water_height DESC NULLS LAST) — stable total ordering across all events by magnitude then water height; no ties (unique per row).
params.metric: rank_by_magnitude_desc_by_year = DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY primary_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST) | rank_by_maxwaterht_desc_by_year = DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY maximum_water_height DESC NULLS LAST) | rank_by_deaths_desc_by_year = DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY deaths DESC NULLS LAST) | rank_by_damage_desc_by_year = DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY total_damage_in_millions_dollars DESC NULLS LAST) | global_rownum_by_mag_water = ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY primary_magnitude DESC NULLS LAST, maximum_water_height DESC NULLS LAST)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to event-level dimensions or lookups that are strictly one-row-per-event on id (for example, if you have another normalized event view keyed 1:1 by id) using: JOIN ... ON tsunami_topmeasures_rank.id = other_event_view.id — safe because tsunami_topmeasures_rank is one row per event (grain = id) so measures/row-level attributes are not duplicated. | Safe to join to tables keyed by year on year when the other side is one-row-per-year (or aggregated to one-row-per-year). Example: join to a per-year summary table on year — safe because the year key on the other side must be aggregated to one row per year to avoid duplication of event rows. | Do NOT join directly to one-to-many detail tables (for example, an event reports table, multiple observation points per event, or any table where multiple rows share the same event id) without first aggregating the detail table to one row per event or otherwise handling multiplicity. Such joins will multiply tsunami_topmeasures_rank rows and will duplicate its rank/rownum measures, producing incorrect counts or sums. | If you need to enrich with many-to-many or one-to-many child records (e.g., event reports, eyewitnesses, station observations), either: a) aggregate the child table to one row per event (compute counts/summaries) and then join on id, or b) join and then re-aggregate with explicit group by id and recompute any measures (do not rely on rank columns as aggregatable metrics). | When composing further ranking or window calculations that partition by year (or other dimensions), prefer to base them on this view's numeric columns (primary_magnitude, maximum_water_height, deaths, total_damage_in_millions_dollars) and treat the precomputed rank columns as attributes for filtering or display only — do not perform arithmetic aggregations over the dense-rank columns expecting additive behavior. | Be cautious joining on country: tsunami_topmeasures_rank has country at event-grain (one row per event). Joining to a country-level aggregation (one row per country) on country is safe (one-to-one or many events to one country) only if you accept event row multiplicity by country (this preserves event rows). However, joining to a country->multiple-rows dimension (e.g., region subdivisions) without aggregation may multiply rows — aggregate first. | Linking to other RANK/AGG sibling views: you may join on id or year as long as the sibling view is also one-row-per-event (same key) or is aggregated to the same grain. Views with different grains (per-box, per-month, per-observation) must be aggregated or joined carefully as above.

tsunami_topmeasures_rank.description: Assigns dense ranks per partition for several severity measures (primary_magnitude, maximum_water_height, deaths, total_damage_in_millions_dollars). Expose rank columns so callers can request top-K by filtering rank <= K downstream. | Use for: Top-K events per year by magnitude / water height / deaths / damage; Selecting event subsets for detailed inspection (e.g., top events within a year); Comparing ranks across measures for the same event

tsunami_events_cumulative_win_by_year_co.name: tsunami_events_cumulative_win_by_year_country
tsunami_events_cumulative_win_by_year_co.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  country,
  COUNT(1) AS events_in_year,
  SUM(COALESCE(deaths,0)) AS deaths_in_year,
  SUM(SUM(COALESCE(deaths,0))) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_deaths_by_country,
  SUM(COUNT(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS cumulative_events_by_country
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event`
GROUP BY year, country

params.description: Per-country, per-year counts and sums of tsunami events and deaths, plus running (cumulative) totals of events and deaths by country over years.
params.when_to_use: Get number of tsunami events and deaths for each country in a specific year (year, country level). | Trend analysis of cumulative deaths or cumulative event counts for a country across years (time-series by year). | As a pre-aggregated building block when composing higher-level reports that need per-country yearly totals or country-level running totals (e.g., plot cumulative deaths over time by country). | Joining to country- or year-dimension tables to add labels or attributes without changing numeric measures (one-to-one joins on country and/or year).
params.output_schema: year: calendar year (derived from the base table column `year` in bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event). | country: country name/code (derived from the base table column `country` in bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event). | events_in_year: number of rows (events) in that year and country = COUNT(1) aggregated from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event. | deaths_in_year: sum of deaths in that year and country = SUM(COALESCE(deaths,0)) aggregated from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event. | cumulative_deaths_by_country: running sum of deaths for the country up to and including the year = SUM(SUM(COALESCE(deaths,0))) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW). | cumulative_events_by_country: running count of events for the country up to and including the year = SUM(COUNT(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW).
params.metric: events_in_year = COUNT(1) -- count of event rows per (year, country) from historical_source_event | deaths_in_year = SUM(COALESCE(deaths,0)) -- sum of deaths per (year, country) with nulls treated as 0 | cumulative_deaths_by_country = SUM(deaths_in_year) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) -- running total of deaths by country across ordered years (computed via window over the aggregated deaths_in_year) | cumulative_events_by_country = SUM(events_in_year) OVER (PARTITION BY country ORDER BY year ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) -- running total of events by country across ordered years (computed via window over the aggregated events_in_year)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a country dimension (e.g., a countries or stations_dim-like view keyed by country) on country — safe because this view is one row per (year,country); joining a 1-row-per-country dimension will not duplicate measures. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a year dimension on year — safe because this view has one row per (year,country); joining a 1-row-per-year dimension will not duplicate measures. | unsafe-to-join without re-aggregation: do NOT join directly to any table or view that is one-to-many from (year,country) (for example, raw event-level detail like tsunami_events_core_sel or events_point_reports_normalized) without first aggregating that side to (year,country). Doing so will multiply events_in_year, deaths_in_year and the cumulative measures because this view already contains aggregated counts/sums per (year,country). | unsafe-to-join without re-aggregation: do NOT join to other time-series or per-event tables that contain multiple rows per (year,country) (for example per-report or per-observation tables such as events_point_reports_normalized, historical_runups_core_sel) unless you aggregate those tables to the same grain (year,country) and then join on (year,country). | when composing higher-level aggregates (e.g., totals by country across multiple years or regional aggregations), re-aggregate this view's events_in_year and deaths_in_year (SUM) after joining/filtering. For cumulative metrics: cumulative_* are pre-computed at the per-year ordering; if you aggregate away year (e.g., sum over years or collapse to country-level), compute new aggregations from events_in_year/deaths_in_year rather than summing cumulative_* values (summing cumulative values will be incorrect). | window ordering note: cumulative_* rely on ordering by year. If you join and then reorder or change year semantics (e.g., fiscal year), recompute cumulative metrics from the base per-year aggregates to ensure correct ordering.

tsunami_events_cumulative_win_by_year_co.description: Compute running (cumulative) totals of events and deaths by year for each country. Useful for cumulative impact charts and year-over-year comparisons. | Use for: Cumulative deaths/events over time per country; Compute year-to-date impacts for dashboards; Compare growth rates in cumulative impacts between countries

tsunami_events_magnitude_unpivot.name: tsunami_events_magnitude_unpivot
tsunami_events_magnitude_unpivot.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  year,
  country,
  location_name,
  'primary_magnitude' AS magnitude_type,
  primary_magnitude AS magnitude_value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  id,
  year,
  country,
  location_name,
  'abe' AS magnitude_type,
  abe AS magnitude_value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  id,
  year,
  country,
  location_name,
  'iida' AS magnitude_type,
  iida AS magnitude_value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event`
UNION ALL
SELECT
  id,
  year,
  country,
  location_name,
  'soloviev' AS magnitude_type,
  soloviev AS magnitude_value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event`
grain: id, magnitude_type -- one row per event per magnitude-type

params.description: One-row-per-tsunami-event-per-magnitude-type unpivot of multiple magnitude measures so you can analyze, filter, aggregate and join tsunami event magnitudes by magnitude type.
params.when_to_use: Compare or aggregate magnitudes across different magnitude types for tsunami events (e.g., average primary_magnitude vs abe). | Filter events by a specific magnitude_type and then join to event-level details or spatial dimensions. | Build time-series or country-level aggregates of magnitude values by magnitude_type (e.g., yearly average magnitude per country per magnitude_type). | Pivot back into a wide form by magnitude_type or feed into ranking/percentile calculations that operate over a single magnitude column.
params.output_schema: id: unique event identifier — derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.id | year: event year — derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.year | country: event country designation — derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.country | location_name: textual location/place name for the event — derived from bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event.location_name | magnitude_type: the source/type label for this row's magnitude value (one of 'primary_magnitude', 'abe', 'iida', 'soloviev') — assigned literal in the view | magnitude_value: numeric magnitude value corresponding to magnitude_type — derived from the respective base column in bigquery-public-data.noaa_tsunami.historical_source_event (primary_magnitude, abe, iida, or soloviev)
params.metric: magnitude_value = direct passthrough of the base magnitude column selected per union arm (no additional aggregation or transformation). | There are no pre-computed aggregates in this view; it is a reshaped (unpivot) representation that normalizes multiple magnitude columns into (magnitude_type, magnitude_value) rows.
params.composition: Join safely (one-to-one or many-to-one) to tsunami_events_core_sel (SEL) on id — safe because this view is one row per (id, magnitude_type). Joining on id to a one-row-per-event table will not duplicate event-level attributes; however note that each event may appear multiple times here for different magnitude_type values. | Join safely to event-level dimension tables keyed by id (for example any event-level enrichment that has at most one row per event id) — safe because those dims are one-row-per-id so they won't multiply rows beyond the existing per-(id,magnitude_type) grain. | When aggregating measures from this view, group by id if you need event-level uniqueness, or group by (id, magnitude_type) to preserve the view grain. For country/year-level aggregates over magnitude_value, aggregate magnitude_value directly and include magnitude_type in the group if you want type-specific metrics. | Do NOT join this view directly to any table/view that is one-to-many keyed to id (for example a table of multiple reports, multiple observations, or multiple runups per event) without first aggregating the many-side or deduplicating, because such a join will multiply the magnitude_value rows and distort aggregates. If you must join to a one-to-many table, either: |   - aggregate the one-to-many table to one row per event id before joining (e.g., take max/min/count/avg of the many-side), or |   - pre-aggregate this view to one row per id (e.g., compute MAX(CASE WHEN magnitude_type='primary_magnitude' THEN magnitude_value END) ...) before joining so joins remain cardinality-safe. | Do NOT join to other RESHAPE/UNPIVOT views that are also multiple-rows-per-id on id without re-aggregation first — combining multiple unpivoted views by id may produce a Cartesian-like multiplication across their unpivoted rows unless you aggregate to a common grain first.

tsunami_events_magnitude_unpivot.description: Unpivot different stored magnitude-related measures into a long form (magnitude_type, magnitude_value). Useful when analyses need to consider or compare multiple magnitude-like fields (primary_magnitude, abe, iida, soloviev). | Use for: Compare distributions of different magnitude measures; Select the largest magnitude across types per event; Aggregate magnitudes by type across regions or years

storm_event_year_state_counts.name: storm_event_year_state_counts
storm_event_year_state_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM TIMESTAMP(event_begin_time)) AS calendar_year,
  state AS state,
  COUNT(1) AS event_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1950' AND '2024'
  AND event_begin_time IS NOT NULL
  AND state IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY calendar_year, state
storm_event_year_state_counts.description: Event counts aggregated to one row per calendar year and state (full state name). Also exposes the extracted year for easy joins and per-year ranking. This view does NOT apply top-k filtering; it provides per-year per-state counts that can be ranked/filtered later.

state_name_to_postal.name: state_name_to_postal
state_name_to_postal.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical full state name as used in storms data
  state AS state,
  -- 2-letter postal abbreviation (lifted from a trusted external reference; literals left here intentionally for view stability)
  CASE
    WHEN state IN ('Alabama') THEN 'AL'
    WHEN state IN ('Alaska') THEN 'AK'
    WHEN state IN ('Arizona') THEN 'AZ'
    WHEN state IN ('Arkansas') THEN 'AR'
    WHEN state IN ('California') THEN 'CA'
    WHEN state IN ('Colorado') THEN 'CO'
    WHEN state IN ('Connecticut') THEN 'CT'
    WHEN state IN ('Delaware') THEN 'DE'
    WHEN state IN ('District of Columbia','D.C.','DC') THEN 'DC'
    WHEN state IN ('Florida') THEN 'FL'
    WHEN state IN ('Georgia') THEN 'GA'
    WHEN state IN ('Hawaii') THEN 'HI'
    WHEN state IN ('Idaho') THEN 'ID'
    WHEN state IN ('Illinois') THEN 'IL'
    WHEN state IN ('Indiana') THEN 'IN'
    WHEN state IN ('Iowa') THEN 'IA'
    WHEN state IN ('Kansas') THEN 'KS'
    WHEN state IN ('Kentucky') THEN 'KY'
    WHEN state IN ('Louisiana') THEN 'LA'
    WHEN state IN ('Maine') THEN 'ME'
    WHEN state IN ('Maryland') THEN 'MD'
    WHEN state IN ('Massachusetts') THEN 'MA'
    WHEN state IN ('Michigan') THEN 'MI'
    WHEN state IN ('Minnesota') THEN 'MN'
    WHEN state IN ('Mississippi') THEN 'MS'
    WHEN state IN ('Missouri') THEN 'MO'
    WHEN state IN ('Montana') THEN 'MT'
    WHEN state IN ('Nebraska') THEN 'NE'
    WHEN state IN ('Nevada') THEN 'NV'
    WHEN state IN ('New Hampshire') THEN 'NH'
    WHEN state IN ('New Jersey') THEN 'NJ'
    WHEN state IN ('New Mexico') THEN 'NM'
    WHEN state IN ('New York') THEN 'NY'
    WHEN state IN ('North Carolina') THEN 'NC'
    WHEN state IN ('North Dakota') THEN 'ND'
    WHEN state IN ('Ohio') THEN 'OH'
    WHEN state IN ('Oklahoma') THEN 'OK'
    WHEN state IN ('Oregon') THEN 'OR'
    WHEN state IN ('Pennsylvania') THEN 'PA'
    WHEN state IN ('Rhode Island') THEN 'RI'
    WHEN state IN ('South Carolina') THEN 'SC'
    WHEN state IN ('South Dakota') THEN 'SD'
    WHEN state IN ('Tennessee') THEN 'TN'
    WHEN state IN ('Texas') THEN 'TX'
    WHEN state IN ('Utah') THEN 'UT'
    WHEN state IN ('Vermont') THEN 'VT'
    WHEN state IN ('Virginia') THEN 'VA'
    WHEN state IN ('Washington') THEN 'WA'
    WHEN state IN ('West Virginia') THEN 'WV'
    WHEN state IN ('Wisconsin') THEN 'WI'
    WHEN state IN ('Wyoming') THEN 'WY'
    -- include common alternate spellings/entries mapped to their canonical abbreviations
    WHEN state IN ('Commonwealth of Pennsylvania') THEN 'PA'
    WHEN state IN ('Puerto Rico') THEN 'PR'
    WHEN state IN ('Guam') THEN 'GU'
    WHEN state IN ('American Samoa') THEN 'AS'
    WHEN state IN ('U.S. Virgin Islands','Virgin Islands') THEN 'VI'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS state_abbreviation
FROM
  -- use storms wildcard to expose the semantic mapping alongside the storms state vocabulary;
  -- the view has one row per distinct state value present in the source
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT state
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.noaa_historic_severe_storms.storms_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1950' AND '2024'
      AND state IS NOT NULL
  )
state_name_to_postal.description: Canonical mapping of US state full names to 2-letter postal abbreviations. Intended as a stable semantic lookup used when outputs or groupings require postal codes. This view should be implemented/maintained from a trusted external reference table; here it's declared as a semantic mapping (no grain in the storms data).

stations_core.name: stations_core
stations_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(usaf AS STRING) AS usaf,
  CAST(wban AS STRING) AS wban,
  CAST(name AS STRING) AS name,
  CAST(country AS STRING) AS country,
  CAST(state AS STRING) AS state,
  CAST(lat AS FLOAT64) AS lat,
  CAST(lon AS FLOAT64) AS lon,
  CAST(elev AS STRING) AS elev,
  CAST(begin AS STRING) AS begin,
  CAST(`end` AS STRING) AS `end`
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations`
stations_core.description: Canonical, cleaned projection of GSOD stations with core identifying and period-of-record columns. Casts/normalizes column names and exposes begin/end as ISO date strings for downstream date arithmetic.

stations_core_51.name: stations_core_51
stations_core_51.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key/id columns (keep original identifiers)
  stations.usaf AS usaf,
  stations.wban AS wban,

  -- core metadata (canonicalized names to match required output aliases)
  -- prefer trimmed non-empty values; fall back to NULL when blank strings present
  NULLIF(TRIM(stations.name), '') AS name,
  NULLIF(TRIM(stations.country), '') AS country,
  NULLIF(TRIM(stations.state), '') AS state,
  NULLIF(TRIM(stations.call), '') AS call,

  -- geographic fields: cast to FLOAT64 where appropriate, treat non-numeric/empty as NULL
  -- lat/lon in source are FLOAT64 already per DDL; preserve them
  stations.lat AS lat,
  stations.lon AS lon,

  -- elevation: source is STRING; normalize to a consistent numeric-ish string where possible,
  -- but keep as string per requested output column type. Trim blanks and map empty to NULL.
  NULLIF(TRIM(stations.elev), '') AS elev,

  -- begin / end: keep as-is from source, trim blanks to NULL
  NULLIF(TRIM(stations.begin), '') AS begin,
  NULLIF(TRIM(stations.`end`), '') AS `end`
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_gsod.stations` AS stations
stations_core_51.description: Canonicalized station records: one row per station identifier (USAF + WBAN) with core metadata and cleaned geographic/elevation fields.
